  "office_action": "Examiner Action (Non‑Final)\n\nSummary\nThis non‑final action addresses the applicant’s May 29, 2015 response to the Examiner’s March 16, 2015 non‑final Office action. The application remains under pre‑AIA examination. The Office maintained the prior rejections (35 U.S.C. 102(b) and 103(a)) on the present record and raises follow‑up 35 U.S.C. 112(b) points for clarification. The following explains the Examiner’s position and identifies what is required to advance prosecution.\n\n1) Procedural / Status\n- The application remains subject to the earlier Office action (dated March 16, 2015) and to this follow‑up action. Applicant canceled claim 7 and amended claims 1, 8, 9 and 20. The Examiner has reviewed the amendments and argument presented in the May 29, 2015 filing.\n- This action maintains the rejections discussed below. Applicant’s arguments and amendments are addressed point‑by‑point. Where the applicant’s amendment or argument overcomes a specific ground, that ground will be withdrawn. Where the record continues to support a rejection, that rejection is maintained and the basis is explained.\n\n2) 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (Indefiniteness / Claim Clarity)\n- Background: The March 16, 2015 Office action rejected claims 7–11 and 20 under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (pre‑AIA second paragraph) for indefiniteness. The Office explained that claim 7 appeared self‑contradictory (asserting both 'axes disposed at approximately 90° to one another' and 'parallel axes of rotation') and that claim 20 lacked antecedent basis for 'the pair of connection pins'.\n- Applicant’s May 29, 2015 response canceled claim 7 and amended claim 20 to read: \"...each of the first pair and second pair of attachment holes are configured to receive a pair of connection pins of the release assembly...\" The Examiner notes this amendment remedies the antecedent basis issue previously raised for claim 20.\n- Status and Further Requirement: Claim 7 cancellation resolves that particular 112 concern. The antecedent issue in claim 20 is addressed by the amendment and the Examiner will withdraw that portion of the indefiniteness objection regarding antecedent basis. However, the earlier Office action also identified potential ambiguity about whether the claimed \"release assembly disposed at a distal end ... actuatable from a proximal end\" is adequately defined as a single assembly in the claims and supported in the specification. The specification (as filed) describes multiple embodiments of release assemblies (leaf‑spring cam blocks, alternate wire‑spring versions, slack removal assembly, release button and cable, etc.). To resolve any remaining clarity issue, the Examiner requires applicant to either:\n  a) Identify specific, enabling support in the specification (by paragraph numbers and figure numbers) that expressly links the claimed single element \"release assembly\" (with pins) to the proximate actuation elements (release button, release cable, slack removal assembly) so there is no ambiguity as to what is meant by the release assembly and how it is actuated from the proximal end; OR\n  b) Amend the independent claim language to more clearly recite the structural elements of the release assembly (for example, \"a release assembly comprising: a pair of diametrically opposed connection pins ...; a release lever; a release cable extending to a proximal release button\"), if such detailed claim drafting is supported by the specification.\n\n- Action Requested (112): On reply, either provide pinpoint support in the specification for the claim phrasing \"release assembly disposed at a distal end ... actuatable from a proximal end\" (cite specific paragraphs and figures), or submit a claim amendment clarifying the structural components of the release assembly consistent with the written description.\n\n3) 35 U.S.C. 102(b) Rejection — Anticipation by Whitman (US 2009/0101629)\n- Claims Rejected: Claims 1–6 and 13–20 were rejected as anticipated by Whitman. Applicant’s response argued Whitman does not disclose the release assembly limitation newly added to claim 1 and that Whitman shows a permanently coupled end effector.\n- Examiner Position: The Examiner's March 16, 2015 action characterized Whitman as disclosing (inter alia) a distal connection hub with attachment holes and attachment pins offset 90°, a gear train across a pivoting neck, output gears with coupling sockets to receive an end effector drive axle, rotation of the drive shaft resulting in rotation of both output gears, and straight and angled configurations between 0° and 90°. The Office action included the statement: \"Whitman et al. further discloses a pair of holes 553 offset by 90 degrees from a second pair of holes 552 for attaching the end effector and able to receive attachment pins (Fig. 4C).\" The Office's characterization forms the basis for the maintained 102 rejection. The applicant has not submitted specific passages of Whitman showing the absence of any release structure nor shown that the particular distal‑end, proximal‑actuated release assembly recited in amended claim 1 is not disclosed in Whitman’s mounting/attachment arrangements.\n- Requirement / Options: To overcome the anticipation rejection, applicant must either:\n  a) Persuasively show, by citation to the Whitney publication or other admissible evidence, that Whitman does not disclose the specific release assembly feature added to claim 1 (i.e., a distal release assembly that is actuatable from the proximal end of the shaft), or\n  b) Amend the claim to include structural features that are not disclosed in Whitman (for example, a proximal slack removal spring element arranged in a particular way, or a particular cable‑and‑cam arrangement explicitly described in the present specification but absent from Whitman), and point to explicit support in the specification for any added features; or\n  c) If applicant believes the Examiner’s characterization of Whitman is factually incorrect, present specific citations to Whitman demonstrating the alleged factual error.\n\n- Note: The Examiner's factual summary of Whitman in the earlier action is part of the record. If applicant provides contrary evidence (for example, a copy of the Whitman publication annotated to show no proximal actuation or no release pins), the Examiner will consider it and reassess the rejection.\n\n4) 35 U.S.C. 103(a) Rejection — Claim 12 as Unpatentable over Whitman in View of Racenet\n- Rejection Basis: Claim 12 recites the articulation rod and link arrangement. The Office found Whitman did not explicitly disclose the articulated rod/link detail called for by claim 12 and cited Racenet as teaching a rod/link articulation system. The Examiner concluded that a person of ordinary skill would have combined Racenet’s articulation teachings with Whitman’s shaft/end effector arrangement.\n- Applicant’s Argument: Applicant asserted Racenet fails to teach a release assembly and therefore cannot cure Whitman’s deficiencies. The Examiner notes the 103 combination was directed to supplying the articulation rod/link — not to supplying the release assembly. The rejection is premised on adding the rod/link teaching of Racenet to Whitman’s disclosure. Because the record shows Racenet discloses an articulation rod/link, the Examiner maintained the 103 rejection on that ground.\n- Requirement / Options: If applicant contends the combination is improper (lack of motivation to combine, structural incompatibility, or teachings away), applicant should explain with technical reasoning and, if available, supporting evidence. Alternatively, applicant may amend claim 12 to claim structural details that are not in Racenet or to include dependent features that distinguish over the combination.\n\n5) Examiner Requests to Applicant\n- For the 112 matter: Provide pinpoint support for the claimed \"release assembly ... actuatable from a proximal end\" (spec paragraph/figure citations), or amend the claims to recite the specific structural components of the release assembly that are supported by the specification.\n- For the 102 rejection: If applicant contends Whitman does not disclose the claimed release assembly, present specific citations to Whitman (or other admissible evidence) showing the absence of that feature, or amend the claims to recite structural details absent from Whitman and supported by the specification.\n- For the 103 rejection of claim 12: If applicant disagrees with the combination rationale, present technical arguments or evidence why a person skilled in the art would not have combined the references, or amend claim 12 to recite distinguishing structural features.\n\n6) Summary of Examiner's Determination (what is maintained and what is withdrawn)\n- Maintained (for now): The rejections under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b) of claims 1–6 and 13–20 as anticipated by Whitman (US 2009/0101629) are maintained on the present record. The 103 rejection of claim 12 over Whitman in view of Racenet (US 2008/0105730) is maintained on the present record. The prior 112 concern regarding claim 7 is moot because claim 7 has been canceled by applicant. The antecedent portion of the 112 objection regarding claim 20 is withdrawn because applicant amended claim 20 to include 'a pair of connection pins'; however, the Examiner maintains a procedural 112 inquiry requiring either citation support or clarifying amendment tying the claimed 'release assembly' to the described proximal actuation elements. No new prior‑art references are being cited in this action.\n\n7) Next Steps / Reply Guidance\n- Applicant should reply by either:\n  • Submitting specific citation(s) from Whitman proving the cited structural elements are absent (if applicant contends the Examiner’s characterization is incorrect), and/or\n  • Amending claims to recite distinctive structural features absent from Whitman and Racenet (with specification support) and explaining how these amendments overcome the references, and/or\n  • Providing technical arguments and/or evidence why Racenet and Whitman should not be combined (for the 103 rejection) or why the combination would not produce the claimed arrangement.\n- For the 112 issue, provide explicit written‑description locations supporting the claim language or amend the claim to recite the release assembly structural details that are supported.\n\nIf the applicant files responsive amendments and/or arguments that adequately traverse the maintained rejections and address the 112 support/clarity request, the Examiner will consider withdrawal of the maintained rejections. If applicant does not reply within the statutory time period, the current rejections will be made final in a subsequent Office action.\n\nExaminer availability: The Examiner indicated availability and contact information in the prior Office action. If applicant believes a discussion would aid in resolving the outstanding matters, request an interview and include proposed times.\n\nConclusion\n- The Examiner maintains the prior rejections on the current record. Applicant is invited to submit the requested citations, arguments, or claim amendments to resolve the outstanding issues. The Examiner is willing to discuss the matters during an interview if requested.\n\n",
  "limitations": [
    "The Examiner's maintained 102 and 103 rejections rely on the characterization of Whitman (US 2009/0101629) and Racenet (US 2008/0105730) provided in the March 16, 2015 Office action. The Examiner's statements about those references are taken from the Office action text in the record; the full text of the cited references is not reproduced here. If applicant provides contrary evidence (e.g., specific cited passages in Whitman showing absence of a release assembly), the Examiner will reconsider.",
    "The record does not include an explicit verbatim quote from Whitman or Racenet showing all structural correspondences; the Office action paraphrases figures and elements. Applicant should submit precise citations to specific lines/figures of the printed publications if arguing the Examiner’s characterization is incorrect."
  ]

claim_ground_evidence.rationale: The Examiner's prior rejection under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b) cited Whitman et al. (US 2009/0101629). The applicant amended claim 1 to add a release assembly limitation but the record (the Office action) indicates Whitman discloses an interfacing distal hub with holes and attachment pins and gear/drive structures that correspond to the claimed elements. Specifically, the claim language still contains unclear phraseology and functional terms that leave uncertainty as to metes and bounds: (1) "hat brim ... for shielding" remains indefinite because the scope (structural limitation of the brim vs. intended function) is not clearly bounded by claim language; (2) "receives the debris" remains ambiguous as to whether the cover "absorbs," "contacts," "overlies," or merely is positioned to catch debris — this affects the structural requirements of the cover and how to assess infringement and novelty; (3) the continued use of phrases like "so in such a way" and "in use" without defining what structure performs the recited effect leaves claim scope unclear. Regarding obviousness over Karlsson (and the cited combinations), the Examiner maintains the original 103 findings. Karlsson explicitly discloses a cap/cover attached to the visor and helmet with front attachments and an elastic rear ribbon that biases the cap rearwards/upwards (see record). Irrgang and Stokes teach multi-section covers and reflective materials respectively. Applicant's arguments asserting lack of motivation to combine are not persuasive because applying known multi-section construction (Irrgang) or reflective ornamentation (Stokes) to a cap/cover arrangement such as Karlsson would have been within the ordinary skill in the art for the predictable result identified by the references themselves. The Examiner also notes Applicant has not provided objective evidence (e.g., experimental data, secondary considerations) that rebuts the prima facie case of obviousness nor has Applicant identified persuasive non-hindsight reasons in the prior art that would preclude the asserted combinations.

parsed.office_action:
Examiner Action (Non-Final) — Response to Applicant A1 and Amended Claims
Summary
The Examiner has considered Applicant's response dated April 17, 2017 (A1), the filed claim amendments, and the prior Office action dated February 27, 2017 (O1). For the reasons below, the Examiner maintains the rejections under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (indefiniteness) and 35 U.S.C. 103 (obviousness) as set forth in the February 27, 2017 Office action. The Applicant's amendments and remarks have been considered but are not sufficient to overcome the identified grounds of rejection. The Applicant is advised of the specific deficiencies and the basis for maintaining the rejections, and is invited to further amend the claims or present argument and evidence addressing the points below.
I. Status of Claims
Claims 1–20 as originally presented were rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) in O1 and many claims were rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 over Karlsson and combinations. Applicant filed amended claims (document J1MNMJKBRXEAPX0) and added new claim 21. The amendments are entered for consideration to the extent they are responsive to the outstanding non-final action. However, the prior rejections are maintained for reasons explained below.
II. 35 U.S.C. 112(b) — Indefiniteness (Claims 1–20 maintained)
Background and prior finding: In the February 27, 2017 Office action, claims 1–20 were rejected as indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the claimed subject matter (O1). Specific examples in O1 included ambiguity surrounding phrases such as "the hat brim being configured to shield, at least in part, eyes of a user," the meaning of "receives" with respect to debris, and claim phrasing using "in such a way." The Office action explained that those recitations did not clearly set forth the metes and bounds of the claimed invention.
Applicant's amendments and arguments: Applicant amended claims (entered as currently amended in the record) and argues the amendments derive from the specification, that wording such as "in such a way" and "configured to" are permissible, and cites case law about claim construction and the permissible use of functional language.
Examination and determination: The Examiner recognizes that claim drafting may employ functional expressions such as "configured to" and that functional language is not per se improper. However, 35 U.S.C. 112(b) requires claims to distinctly claim the subject matter regarded as the invention. The present claim set contains multiple limitations that remain ambiguous as to the structural boundaries to be enforced. Examples include:
- "hat brim for shielding, at least in part, eyes of a user from debris" — This recitation mixes an apparent structural element ("hat brim") with a broad functional result ("for shielding"). The claim does not define any structural features of the brim that limit the scope (e.g., geometry, location, structure) beyond its ordinary dictionary meaning. It is unclear whether Applicant asserts a particular structural brim design or merely calls any helmet brim "for shielding." Without clearer structural limitations or claim context, this phrase impedes clear notice to the public and reliable claim construction.
- "the cover assembly receives the debris" / "receives the debris being directed, at least in part, to the front ..." — The claim term "receives" is susceptible to multiple plausible interpretations (e.g., absorbent, overlies and retains, deflects, contacts). Each interpretation could implicate different structures and produce different claim scope. The amendment does not identify the structural feature that performs the receiving function (e.g., 'a pocket that captures particulate debris' or 'a sheet positioned to intercept falling debris and permit particles to fall away from the brim').
- Continued use of phrases such as "so in such a way" or "in such a way" that tie functional results to claim scope without identifying the structural elements that produce that result exacerbate the lack of clarity. The fact that the Applicant cites cases addressing the permissible use of "configured to" or "adapted to" does not automatically convert the present functional recitations into definite structural claim elements. The precedents cited (e.g., Giannelli) show that context and specification support are decisive: functional phrasing must be supported and reasonably limited by the specification so that PHOSITA can determine the claimed boundaries.
Conclusion under 112(b): For the reasons above and as previously identified in O1, the Examiner finds that the amendments do not resolve the indefinite limitations. Therefore, the 35 U.S.C. 112(b) rejection of claims 1–20 is maintained. Applicant may wish to amend claims to recite the structure that performs the recited functions (for example, replacing ambiguous functional phrases with structural limitations disclosed in the specification and drawings) or provide claim definitions/clarifying language in the specification that clearly tie functional language to specific structure.
Representative record support: The prior Office action sets forth the basis for the 112 rejection: "Claims 1- 20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) ... as being indefinite ..." (O1). Applicant's amended claim language still recites functional phrases such as "so in such a way that the cover assembly receives the debris" (J1MNMJKBRXEAPX0).
III. 35 U.S.C. 103 — Obviousness (maintained over Karlsson and combinations)
Background and prior finding: The Office action dated February 27, 2017 rejected many claims under 35 U.S.C. 103 as unpatentable over Karlsson (US 4,547,908), and, for claims directed to multi-section covers or reflective material, in view of Irrgang and Stokes respectively (O1). The Examiner relied upon explicit disclosures in Karlsson showing a cap/cover attached to a visor and a helmet with front attachments and an elastic rear ribbon that biases the cap (see record quotations in O1).
Applicant's arguments: Applicant traversed the rejections, arguing (inter alia) that: (1) Karlsson does not teach the claimed front/rear/first/second/third bracket relationships as claimed; (2) the Examiner improperly applied hindsight and failed to provide adequate motivation to combine references; and (3) the functional terms are structural limitations and should be given weight. Applicant additionally asserts that the amendments and added detail distinguish over the cited art.
Examination and determination: The Examiner has reconsidered the cited references in light of Applicant's arguments and the amended claims. The record supports the Examiner's original position that Karlsson discloses a cap/cover attached to a helmet and visor, front attachments (clamps/pins), and an elastic ribbon at the rear edge that attaches to helmet-side mountings such that the cap is biased rearwards/upwards (see O1 quoting Karlsson). Those disclosures correspond to many of the claimed features: a cover assembly attached to a visor/face-shield bracket assembly and a rear attachment that biases the cover relative to the helmet. For the pending claims that add multi-section cover structure, Irrgang discloses multi-section connectable cover constructions and sewing arrangements, i.e., the specific arrangement of connectable sections claimed. For reflective material, Stokes discloses reflective portions applied to helmet covers. Combining these teachings to adapt well-known cover sectioning or reflective ornamentation to a visor-mounted cap/cover as in Karlsson would have been within the routine skill of a person having ordinary skill in the art to achieve the predictable result.
On the point of motivation to combine and hindsight: The Office's rejection identifies factual teachings in the cited references that provide reason to combine — Karlsson teaches a visor/cover arrangement; Irrgang teaches well-known multi-section cover construction; Stokes teaches reflective ornamentation. The combination proposed is a predictable application of known cover-sectioning or reflective ornamentation to the visor-mounted cover arrangement disclosed in Karlsson. Applicant's broad assertion of impermissible hindsight is not persuasive because the Examiner's prima facie case cites explicit teaching in the prior art, and Applicant has not provided convincing objective evidence (such as unexpected technical effect, commercial success tied to claimed features, or other secondary considerations) that rebuts the prima facie case. Nor has Applicant identified a technical incompatibility that would have deterred a PHOSITA from making the proposed combinations.
Conclusion under 103: For the above reasons, the Examiner maintains the rejections under 35 U.S.C. 103 as presented in the February 27, 2017 Office action. Applicant's arguments are acknowledged but do not identify persuasive error in the Examiner's factual findings or legal application.
IV. Guidance to Applicant — Suggested Claiming and Evidence to Overcome the Rejections
To address the 112(b) indefiniteness rejection, consider the following (non-exhaustive) approaches:
- Amend claims to recite specific structural features disclosed in the specification and drawings that perform the recited functions. For example, instead of "receives the debris," claim language could recite "a front cover section formed as a sheet extending across and overlying the hat brim so as to capture particulate debris falling towards the brim" or similar structural detail present in the specification.
- Replace or further define functional results (e.g., "for shielding") with structural limitations (e.g., brim geometry, position relative to front hat section, or a recited shield element attached to the brim).
- If functional language is retained, provide explicit claim-supporting definitions in the specification that tie "configured to" language to corresponding structure and equivalents, and then amend claims to incorporate such structure or to refer to the supporting specification paragraphs by reference (bearing in mind 35 U.S.C. 112 requirements).
To address the 103 rejections, consider the following (non-exhaustive) approaches:
- Amend the claims to recite features that are not taught or suggested by the cited art (e.g., particular bracket attachment arrangements, unique structural details of the connector assembly or connectable sections that are not found in Karlsson/Irrgang/Stokes), and ensure those features are clearly supported in the specification.
- Submit persuasive evidence of non-obviousness if available (e.g., comparative data showing unexpected results, long-felt but unsolved need, licensing/commercial success tied to the specific claimed features, recognition by others, technical acclaim). Evidence should specifically tie the claimed inventive features to the asserted secondary considerations.
- If Applicant believes the Examiner misidentified the scope of a cited reference, point to explicit passages or figures in the cited art that support the objection and explain why they do not teach the claimed feature.
V. Next Steps and Period for Reply
This is a non-final action maintaining the previous rejections. Applicant is invited to file a further response within the statutory time period: (a) amend the claims to overcome the 112(b) issues (for example, by reciting clear structural limitations rather than ambiguous functional language); (b) present substantive arguments with supporting evidence to rebut the 103 rejections; and/or (c) present admissible objective evidence of non-obviousness. If Applicant elects to present further amendments, please provide a concise claim listing and indicate any claim(s) to be canceled.
VI. Representative Record Citations
- O1 (Office action dated Feb. 27, 2017): "Claims 1- 20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) ... as being indefinite ..." (IZIQABSZRXEAPX4).
- Karlsson teaching quoted in O1: "A cap arrangement (generally designated 5) extends between the visor 2 and the helmet and consists in this case of a sheet of water-repellant textile fabric. The front edge 6 of the cap arrangement 5 is attached to the upper edge of the visor 2 by means of attachments 8, each consisting of a clamp provided with a pin, holding the front edge 6 of the cap arrangement." (IZIQABSZRXEAPX4 quoting Karlsson).
- Applicant amended claim language showing continued use of functional phrasing: "the connector assembly is configured to connect the cover assembly to the face-shield bracket assembly so in such a way that the cover assembly receives the debris ..." (J1MNMJKBRXEAPX0).
VII. Examiner Contact
If Applicant wishes to discuss the action, telephone contact with the Examiner is allowed. The Examiner's phone number is listed in the file wrapper. Telephone interviews can be an efficient way to narrow issues prior to filing a further response.
Conclusion
The rejections under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) and 35 U.S.C. 103 as set forth in the Office action dated February 27, 2017 are maintained for the reasons stated above. Applicant is invited to further amend the claims and/or present evidence and argument responsive to the specific defects identified above. A reply that does not place the application in condition for allowance will result in a subsequent Office action (which may be final).

If Applicant disputes the Examiner's characterization of those references, Applicant should provide specific prior art citations/paragraphs or file a claim amendment that distinguishes the claimed subject matter over the specific disclosures cited by the Examiner.

This action maintains prior rejections and does not assume subsequent filings or claim entries beyond the amended claims submitted on 2017-04-17; any later-filed amendments or remarks are not considered here.

parsed.office_action:
Summary of action
- Applicant's amendment to independent claim 1 (adding a filament limitation) has been considered. The amendment is entered into the record. The specification provides support for filaments extending from the periphery of the haptic plate (see cited specification language below). The prior 35 U.S.C. 103 rejections over Blake that were applied to claim 1 (and dependent claims 2-6 and 8-9) are withdrawn in light of the entered amendment because the combination of record references relied upon in the earlier Office action did not show the newly added filament limitation.
- The rejection of claim 7 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as unpatentable over Blake in view of Richardson is maintained. The amendment to claim 1 does not overcome the earlier-applied combination for claim 7, which recites a thickness relationship between the haptic plate and connector that the prior Office action found would have been obvious to modify using Richardson's teachings. Applicant may respond by argument or by amendment directed to claim 7 if prosecution is to continue.
Discussion and reasons for action
Entry of amendment to claim 1
Applicant timely filed an amendment on March 4, 2014 that adds the limitation "wherein at least one filament is coupled to the haptic plate extending from a periphery of the haptic plate" to independent claim 1 (document HSDODPBCPXXIFW3). The amendment is supported by the specification. See for example: "the haptic plate has filaments 140a-140d extending from its periphery to help in fixing the haptic plate in a capsular bag" (pgpub_description). Accordingly, the amendment is entered.
Effect on prior 35 U.S.C. 103 rejections
The prior Non-Final Office action (HMALDM6CPXXIFW4, mailed October 4, 2013) rejected claims 1-6 and 8-9 as obvious over Blake (US 2006/0064161), and rejected claim 7 as obvious over Blake in view of Richardson (US 2008/0021550). The earlier rejection of claim 1 relied on Blake as teaching an optic, a haptic plate surrounding the optic, connectors (arms) between the optic and plate, and various plate/connector configurations. The previously applied combination did not identify filaments coupled to the haptic plate extending from the periphery as being disclosed by Blake. Applicant's amendment to claim 1 adds that filament limitation, and the record does not indicate Blake (as applied in the prior Office action) discloses the filaments recited in the amendment. Therefore the Examiner withdraws the earlier 103 rejection for claim 1 and for dependents that rely only on elements present in the newly amended claim 1 (claims 2-6 and 8-9) contingent on the amendment being entered. These claims are now in condition for further consideration for allowance unless new references or issues are presented.
Rejection maintained for claim 7 (35 U.S.C. 103)
Claim 7 recites: "The AIOL of claim 1, wherein the at least one haptic plate has a thickness that is greater than any portion of the at least one connector." The prior Office action applied Blake in view of Richardson to reject claim 7 under 35 U.S.C. 103. The prior action asserts Richardson teaches an accommodative lens in which connectors (arms) are thinner than the haptic plate portions (see HMALDM6CPXXIFW4: "Richardson teaches an accommodative lens ... where the connectors (arms) are thinner than the haptic plate (Fig. 9)"). The Examiner continues to rely on that combination for claim 7 because the amendment to claim 1 (adding filaments) does not alter the plate-versus-connector thickness relationship and does not negate the rationale for combining the two references with respect to the thickness feature. Thus claim 7 remains rejected as obvious over Blake in view of Richardson.
Applicant arguments and next steps
Applicant argued in the remarks accompanying the amendment that Blake fails to teach the filament element now present in claim 1. The Examiner agrees and has entered the amendment. Applicant asserted that dependent claims 2-9 are allowable in view of the amended claim 1; dependent claims 2-6 and 8-9 are withdrawn from rejection contingent upon entry of claim 1. Claim 7, however, remains rejected as explained above.
To advance prosecution, Applicant may:
- File a reply canceling or amending claim 7 to include additional limitations not present in the combination of Blake and Richardson, or
- Present substantive argument explaining why the combination of Blake and Richardson would not have made claim 7 obvious (point to specific teachings/figures/paragraphs in Blake and Richardson and explain why those teachings cannot be combined to yield the plate/connector thickness relationship), or
- Present additional evidence (e.g., contemporaneous expert declaration) showing non-obviousness of claim 7 over the applied combination.
If Applicant instead wishes to request telephonic interview to discuss the maintained rejection and any proposed amendments, the Examiner will entertain scheduling a conference. The Examiner encourages Applicant to identify specific portions of the prior art (with document citations and precise passages) if arguing that the combination is improper.
Claims status after entry
- Claim 1 (as amended): entered; prior 103 rejection withdrawn (see rationale above).
- Claims 2-6, 8-9: dependent on entered claim 1; prior 103 rejections withdrawn contingent on entry of claim 1.
- Claim 7: dependent on claim 1; rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103 over Blake in view of Richardson is maintained.
Support in the record
- Applicant amendment (claim 1 amended): HSDODPBCPXXIFW3, support span: "wherein at least one filament is coupled to the haptic plate extending from a periphery of the haptic plate".
- Specification support for filaments: pgpub_description, support span: "the haptic plate has filaments 140a-140d extending from its periphery to help in fixing the haptic plate in a capsular bag".
- Prior Office action asserting rejections and combination: HMALDM6CPXXIFW4, support spans cited in the record of the prior action.
Conclusion
The amendment to claim 1 is entered. The Examiner withdraws the prior 103 rejections of claim 1 and of dependent claims 2-6 and 8-9 contingent on entry of the amendment. The rejection of claim 7 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as unpatentable over Blake in view of Richardson is maintained. Applicant is invited to respond by argument, by amendment directed to claim 7, or by submission of evidence addressing the maintained rejection. If Applicant believes the maintained rejection is in error, identify the specific portion(s) of Blake and/or Richardson relied upon in the prior Office action and explain why that portion does not support the Examiner's combination rationale.

applicant_argument_responses.response: The examiner notes that withdrawal of the § 102 anticipation rejection based on Lee for the amended independents does not, by itself, require withdrawal of the § 103 rejections for the claims that were rejected under combinations. On the present record, the examiner finds the applied combinations still present a prima facie case of obviousness for the claims to which they were applied: Tsern provides teaching of a DIMM environment and page-table type mapping, and Bhakta teaches virtual-pair copying. Because applicant amended the independent claims to add the overlap limitation, combinations that would still render other claimed subject matter obvious must be addressed claim-by-claim. Applicant's A1 remarks do not supply persuasive evidence or arguments specific to each asserted combination to show non-obviousness (for example, no evidence was submitted showing a technical incompatibility between Lee and Tsern or between Lee and Bhakta, nor a demonstration that the combination would have been non-routine or lacking motivation). Therefore the examiner maintains the § 103 rejections on the dependent and independent claims previously targeted by those combinations. Applicant may rebut the § 103 rejections by: (i) amending the claims to add further distinguishing limitations not taught by the combination of references, and/or (ii) demonstrating (by argument and/or evidence) why a person of ordinary skill would not have been motivated to combine the cited references or why the combination would not yield the claimed subject matter. In particular, to the extent any dependent claim still incorporates the overlap limitation (by dependency), applicant should indicate whether the applied combinations (Lee+Tsern, Lee+Bhakta) disclose or render obvious that overlap feature; if not, applicant may point this out claim-by-claim.

Examiner Communication (Non-Final)
Summary
This Office action responds to the Applicant's filing dated April 18, 2017 (A1) that amends claims and argues against the rejections set forth in the Office action mailed January 27, 2017 (O1). The record documents available as of April 18, 2017 include the prior art references relied upon in O1 (Lee US 2007/0271424; Tsern US 2007/0088995; Bhakta US 2006/0062047), the published specification and claims (PG pub), and Applicant's amended claims and remarks (A1: J1NWFDVRRXEAPX2, J1NWFDVTRXEAPX2). The examiner has considered the amendments and arguments and provides the following determinations and guidance.
1) Amendment and withdrawal of the § 102 anticipation rejection (Lee)
- Applicant amended independent claims 1, 11 and 20 to add a limitation requiring that the first plurality of memory components includes: (a) at least one memory component not included in the second plurality, and (b) at least one other memory component that is also included in the second plurality. This creates a claim requirement that a memory component be a member of both pluralities (an overlap between the pluralities).
- The prior Office action (O1) had rejected the original claims under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) over Lee. O1 relied on Lee's disclosure of multiple memory groups and concurrent read operations. Applicant correctly pointed out in the A1 remarks that Lee's memory groups (MG1, MG2, etc.) are presented as distinct, non-overlapping groups in the cited portions of Lee's disclosure (see Lee Fig. 11 and associated description). The Examiner agrees that, on the present record, Lee as relied upon in O1 does not disclose that a single memory component is a member of two distinct pluralities at the same time — the specific overlap limitation added in the amendments.
- Conclusion: The examiner withdraws the § 102(a) anticipation rejection over Lee for the amended independent claims 1, 11 and 20 (and for claims that directly depend from them and thereby require the same overlap limitation, e.g., claim 6 depends from claim 1). The withdrawal follows the Applicant's amendment which adds a limitation not taught by Lee and the Applicant remarks demonstrating that the limitation is not found in Lee.
2) Status of remaining rejections (35 U.S.C. 103(a) over combinations)
- O1 applied combinations of Lee with Tsern and Lee with Bhakta to reject several dependent and independent claims under 35 U.S.C. 103(a). Those rejections were not predicated on a pure anticipation of the overlap limitation by Lee alone; rather they are combination-based obviousness rejections asserting that the missing teachings can be supplied by the secondary references (Tsern and Bhakta) and that a person of ordinary skill would have been motivated to combine the references for stated reasons (e.g., efficiency, module architecture).
- Applicant's A1 remarks argued generally that Lee does not disclose the overlap and requested withdrawal of the § 103 rejections. The examiner acknowledges that Lee alone does not disclose the overlap limitation, and the § 102 rejection was withdrawn for amended independent claims as set forth above. However, the amendments and Applicant remarks do not persuasively show that the asserted combinations (Lee + Tsern; Lee + Bhakta) fail to render the other claim features obvious, or that the combination is improper or would lack motivation. In the examiner's view, the cited secondary references do supply teachings that are relevant to the dependent claim limitations (for example Tsern teaches buffered DIMM-like module structures and page-table mapping; Bhakta discloses virtual-pair copying behavior). On the present record, the examiner maintains the § 103(a) rejections for the claims previously targeted by those combinations (claims 3, 5, 8, 10, 13, 15, 18, and the others indicated in O1) because they remain prima facie unpatentable over the cited combinations.
- Applicant may respond by (a) presenting claim amendments that add limitations not taught by the applied combination, and/or (b) presenting persuasive argument and/or evidentiary material showing absence of motivation to combine or teaching away, unexpected technical effect, incompatibility between references, or other non-obviousness evidence. The examiner will consider such responses and any supporting evidence you may submit.
3) Specific examiner guidance to address the maintained § 103 rejections
- For claims rejected over Lee + Tsern: identify specifically which claim limitation(s) Applicant contends are not taught or would not have been obvious from the combined disclosures of Lee and Tsern. If the claimed limitation pertains to DIMM coupling, page-table mapping or other module structures, explain with citation to the specification and, if available, evidence or affidavit why the cited combination would not teach or render obvious that limitation.
- For claims rejected over Lee + Bhakta: identify specifically which limitation(s) Applicant contends are not taught by the combination (for example, if the "virtual pair" copying structure or its function as claimed is not taught or is claimed to be implemented in a manner differing from Bhakta, explain and show support).
- If Applicant believes the combination would produce an operability or compatibility problem (e.g., technical incompatibility between the teachings of the references that would have prevented a skilled practitioner from combining them), present argument and supporting evidence (for example, declaration, test data, or authoritative technical literature) showing the incompatibility.
4) Claim form and entry of amendment
- The amended claim text in A1 (J1NWFDVRRXEAPX2) appears in the record. If Applicant wishes to have the amendments entered as filed, the revised claims will be entered and the record updated. Entry of the claims will be accompanied by withdrawal of the § 102 anticipation rejection for amended independent claims and related dependent claims as noted above, but not the maintained § 103 rejections.
- If Applicant wishes to file further amendments, please note that amendment practice and any required disclaimers or remarks should comply with 37 C.F.R. 1.121. After entry of the present amendment, any further amendments to independent claims typically will be treated as a new response and may trigger further reexamination or another Office action.
5) Procedural matters / next steps
- The § 102 anticipation rejection over Lee is withdrawn for amended independent claims 1, 11 and 20 and for dependent claims that require the overlap limitation (e.g., claim 6). The examiner will enter the amended claims if Applicant requests entry (A1 has been received and will be placed in the file). If Applicant elects not to pursue additional amendments and provides no further substantive reply to the maintained § 103 rejections within the statutory period, the examiner may issue a final Office action on the maintained grounds.
- The maintained § 103 rejections are continued in the non-final action. Applicant is invited to reply to the § 103 rejections by: (i) amendment of the rejected claims to include additional limitations not taught by the cited combinations and thereby put the claims in condition for allowance, or (ii) persuasive argument and/or evidence addressing why the combination does not render the claimed invention obvious. Any submitted evidence should be accompanied by an appropriate declaration where required.
- If Applicant wishes to have an examiner interview to discuss claim scope, the maintained rejections and potential amendments, contact the examiner to arrange a convenient time.
6) Examiner contact
If you believe telephone discussion would clarify issues, call the undersigned Examiner at (571) 272-8625. If you are unable to reach the Examiner, call the Examiner's Supervisor, Henry Tsai, at (571) 272-4176.
Limits/uncertainties
- The record does not include materials beyond those explicitly cited in the original Office action and Applicant's A1 submission; if Applicant relies on any evidence not yet of record (for example, declarations, test reports or technical articles), such evidence was not available to the examiner at the time of this action and must be submitted in reply to this action to be considered.
- The examiner has withdrawn the § 102 anticipation rejection only for the amended claims that include the overlap limitation. This withdrawal does not imply allowance of the claims; the maintained § 103 rejections must still be addressed for allowance of affected claims.
Conclusion/Action requested of Applicant
- The § 102(a) rejection over Lee for amended independent claims 1, 11 and 20 and dependent claims that require the overlap limitation is withdrawn. The Examiner will enter the amended claims upon Applicant's request (A1 suffices to present amendment; any request for entry is honored by the Office if the amendment is formally compliant). - The § 103(a) rejections over the cited combinations are maintained for the other claims identified in the earlier Office action (O1). Applicant may respond by argument, amendment, and/or evidence directed to the maintained § 103 grounds. - If Applicant intends to pursue allowance, please reply within the statutory time period with either (a) arguments and/or evidence addressing the maintained § 103 rejections, or (b) amended claim language addressing the deficiencies identified in this action.

Examiner Action (Non-Final)

Summary
- The application has been amended and applicant submitted remarks. Claims 1–20 are pending. Claims 1, 6, 11 and 16 were amended to expressly recite that the prioritizing is performed 'by the user equipment (UE)'. Applicant conceded that claims 6–10 invoke 35 U.S.C. 112(f) and identified corresponding structure in the specification. The examiner has reviewed the amendments and remarks and provides the following determinations and guidance.

35 U.S.C. 112(f) (means-plus-function)
- Status: Withdrawn for claims 6–10.
- Reasoning: The applicant agreed that claims 6–10 invoke 35 U.S.C. 112(f) and has identified corresponding structure in the specification including the communicating module, prioritizing module, processor, computer-readable medium, and the IRAT measurement system described in the specification and illustrated in Figure 7. The examiner previously identified corresponding structure in the Office action and the applicant has provided support pointers (see SPEC). The identification of these structures is sufficient for the means-plus-function elements recited in claims 6–10, therefore the 112(f) interpretation objection is withdrawn for those claims. Claim drafting note: if applicant later adds or modifies the means-plus-function language, ensure that corresponding structure remains present in the specification or add explicit structural/algorithmic details to the claims to avoid recurrence of 112(f) issues.

35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) – Anticipation over Eerolainen
- Status: Maintained for the listed claims (see below).
- Affected claims: 1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 9, 11, 12, 14, 16, 17, 19 (as maintained in the prior Office action).
- Reasoning: The prior Office action identified Eerolainen (U.S. Pub. No. 2008/0176564) as teaching IRAT measurement reporting and teaching prioritized IRAT measurement scheduling. The examiner's prior characterization (O1) indicates Eerolainen discloses prioritized IRAT measurement and reporting measurement data to the network and executing handover. Applicant amended independent claims to add the express limitation that prioritizing is performed 'by the user equipment (UE)' and argues Eerolainen discloses only network-side prioritization. The examiner notes that the prior rejection relied on the examiner's understanding that Eerolainen teaches prioritized IRAT measurement scheduling broadly enough to meet the claim language. The record currently contains the examiner's characterization of Eerolainen as the basis for the rejection but does not include the full Eerolainen text in this file wrapper. Accordingly, the 102(a)(1) rejections are maintained pending a showing by applicant of either (a) a passage from Eerolainen that clearly and explicitly shows the absence of UE-performed prioritization (i.e., a passage that limits prioritization to the network and prevents the UE from performing prioritization), or (b) an amendment to the claims that adds limiting features (structure, specific UE-executed algorithms, data structures, or other details) not disclosed by Eerolainen.
- Applicant action advised: To rebut the maintained 102 rejections in light of the amended 'by the user equipment' language, applicant should either (1) submit the specific passage(s) from Eerolainen showing that prioritization is performed exclusively by the network and not by the UE (with document/page/paragraph citations), or (2) propose claim amendments that recite additional UE-specific structure or algorithm steps for performing the prioritization which are supported by the specification and distinguish over the cited Eerolainen disclosures.

35 U.S.C. 103 – Obviousness over Eerolainen in view of Mark
- Status: Maintained for the listed dependent claims.
- Affected claims: 3, 5, 8, 10, 13, 15, 18, 20.
- Reasoning: The prior Office action combined Eerolainen (teaching prioritized IRAT measurement scheduling) with Mark (teaching varying neighbor-cell measurement monitoring rates and frequencies) to reach the dependent claim limitations that recite increasing or decreasing measurement frequency for certain neighbor cells. In the examiner's view the combination would have been obvious to a person of ordinary skill to obtain the recited measurement-frequency modifications for prioritized neighbor cells. Applicant's remarks do not persuasively show that Mark fails to teach the relevant feature or that the combination is improper. Therefore, the 103 rejections are maintained. Applicant may rebut by pointing to specific disclosure in the applied references that does not support the combination, by providing persuasive factual evidence (e.g., technical incompatibility), or by amending the claims to add further limitations that are not taught or suggested by the cited combination.

Responses to Applicant Arguments (selected)
- Applicant argument (claim 1): Applicant argued Eerolainen discloses network-side prioritization (NW instructs UE measurements) and therefore does not disclose 'prioritizing, by a user equipment (UE), ...' as now claimed. Examiner response: The applicant's argument is noted. The prior rejection relied on the examiner's characterization that Eerolainen discloses prioritized IRAT measurement and scheduling; however, applicant is correct that if Eerolainen only teaches network-side control and does not teach UE-performed prioritization, that factual difference may be material. Because the O1 relied on the examiner's understanding and the full Eerolainen text is not in the record here, applicant is requested to point to the specific Eerolainen passage(s) (document, paragraph, page) that demonstrate that the prioritization is network-only (if applicant wishes to establish that Eerolainen does not read on the amended claim). Alternatively, the applicant may amend claims to include specific, limiting UE-side structure or algorithmic steps for the prioritization that are supported by the specification.
- Applicant argument (claims 6–10 112(f)): Applicant agreed that 112(f) applies and identified corresponding structure in the spec (paragraphs [0050]-[0051], Fig. 7). Examiner response: The specification passages identified by applicant and the examiner's prior identification are sufficient; the 112(f) objection is withdrawn for claims 6–10.

Opportunity to Amend or Present Evidence/Argument
- Applicant is invited to: (1) submit specific cited passages from Eerolainen (and Mark, if relevant) demonstrating noninfringement of the amended claims or lack of teaching for particular limitations; (2) amend claims to add further UE-specific structure or algorithmic detail for the 'by the user equipment' prioritizing limitation; or (3) submit persuasive argument or evidence showing why the combination applied in the 103 rejections is improper or would not render the claimed subject matter obvious.

Conclusion / Next Steps
- The 35 U.S.C. 112(f) issue for claims 6–10 is withdrawn based on applicant's acknowledgement and specification pointers.
- The 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) and 35 U.S.C. 103 rejections identified in the prior Office action are maintained for the listed claims. Applicant should respond with amendments and/or evidence addressing the specific points noted above.
- This is a non-final action. The examiner will consider applicant's response and any submitted evidence or amendments and will either withdraw the maintained rejections or issue a final rejection or allowance, depending on the outcome of prosecution.

Record Citations (for examiner positions in this action)
- O1 (I5FSG7WPPXXIFW4): prior Office action characterizations relied upon for claim rejections.
- SPEC (HMCKN90WPXXIFW3): paragraphs and Fig. 7 cited by applicant as support for UE modules and measurement scheduling behavior.

Limitations
- The record in this file wrapper does not currently include the full text of Eerolainen or Mark as filed in the file wrapper. The examiner has relied on the earlier Office action characterizations of those references. If applicant presents the specific passages from the cited references that are said to be dispositive, the examiner will reconsider the maintained rejections in view of those passages. If applicant prefers, applicant may file copies of the relevant pages of the cited references with precise citations so the examiner can directly compare the claim language with the prior-art text.

applicant_argument_responses.response: Applicant's arguments do not overcome the prior-art identification in the record. The earlier Office action explicitly mapped Solinski and Chen to the claimed structural elements (see HX36BBOVPXXIFW4). That action explains that Solinski and Chen disclose two wheel supports, two wheels with hub portions, latches operable to rotationally lock the wheels, and brake actuating assemblies with cam surfaces that drive latch displacement. Applicant's mere contention that a particular element in Solinski 'differs' is not supported by citation of evidence from Solinski or by a persuasive claim construction limiting the claimed 'rotatable ... cam surfaces' to exclude the cited teaching. Likewise, Applicant's assertion that Chen does not disclose the claimed cable coupling is not supported by citation to an absence in Chen; the prior action states that Chen discloses brake assemblies connected via a linking tube and tube linkage (HX36BBOVPXXIFW4). To overcome the 102 grounds the applicant must either amend claims to recite features that are absent from the cited references or show, with record support (citations to the references or to the present specification), that a cited statement of the examiner is factually incorrect. No such showing has been made in the present response. Consequently the rejections are maintained.

Summary
The A1 filed October 1, 2014 (I0R0EH7OPXXIFW3; I0TKAOF3PXXIFW1; I0TKAOG9PXXIFW1) has been considered. The amendments to the claims set forth in the A1 have been afforded entry and are of record for examination. The previously-issued detailed Office action (CTNF; HX36BBOVPXXIFW4) remains the controlling prior action. After consideration of the applicant's remarks and amended claims, the examiner maintains the rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) identified in the prior Office action for the claims listed below. This communication explains the reasons for maintaining those rejections and addresses the applicant's arguments.
Claims entered
The claim set submitted with the A1 (I0TKAOF3PXXIFW1) has been entered and will be examined. New claims 22–28 have been noted and will be considered where indicated in this action.
Disposition of prior rejections and response to remarks
1) Maintenance of 35 U.S.C. 102(b) rejections
- The prior Office action (HX36BBOVPXXIFW4) rejected claims as anticipated by Solinski (US 2011/0048867) and Chen (US 2012/0031714). The examiner's prior identification mapped the structural elements of the challenged claims to features described in those printed publications. Representative record language identifying the grounds is: "Claims 1, 2, 4, 6, 8-9, 12, 14, 18, 21 are rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b) as being anticipated by Solinski et al. (US 2011/0048867)." (HX36BBOVPXXIFW4).
- Applicant's A1 filing argues that Solinski's shuttle/latch behavior differs from the claimed 'rotatable cam surfaces' causing latch displacements, and that Chen does not show the cable coupling the two actuators as claimed. Those arguments were considered. Applicant has not cited, and the record does not contain, any passage of Solinski or Chen showing the absence of the claimed features relied upon in the prior action, nor has Applicant demonstrated that the prior characterization of those references is factually erroneous. The burden to rebut a prior-art anticipation is to show with record evidence (for example, a citation to the particular teaching in the prior art that does or does not teach the disputed feature, or an amendment that excludes the cited teaching) that the reference does not in fact disclose the claimed limitation. Applicant's assertions in the remarks are not accompanied by such record citations and therefore do not establish error in the prior action. 2) Claims currently maintained under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)
- Solinski-based rejections maintained for claims: 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12, 14, 18, 21. See HX36BBOVPXXIFW4: "Claims 1, 2, 4, 6, 8-9, 12, 14, 18, 21 are rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b) as being anticipated by Solinski et al. (US 2011/0048867)."

applicant_argument_responses.response: The Examiner has considered these points. The record references show the claimed features in combination are prima facie suggested. Action on Applicant's January 30, 2015 response and amendments

Summary
This is a non-final action in response to the applicant's A1 filing (filed 2015-01-30) which amended the claims and argued against the outstanding 35 U.S.C. 103 rejections. The prior Office action (November 3, 2014) set forth rejections of the original claims over Niwamoto in view of Arling, with further citations of Kopf and Yuh for certain dependent claims. The applicant cancelled claim 2 and amended claim language. The record has been reviewed. The Examiner maintains the prior 103 rejections for the reasons below, and addresses claim form defects that must be corrected before further processing toward potential allowance.

1) Status of claims
- Claims pending: 1, 3–15 (per applicant filing). Claim 2 is canceled. The Examiner acknowledges the amendments but observes remaining substantive rejections as indicated below. Several dependent claims contain improper or unclear dependency language that must be corrected (see paragraph 4).

2) Rejection maintained — obviousness under 35 U.S.C. 103
Claims 1 and the indicated dependent claims remain rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as unpatentable over the combinations stated in the November 3, 2014 Office action:
- Claims 1–3, 5, 8–13, 15: Niwamoto (US 7,631,197 B2) in view of Arling (US 2005/0097618 A1).
- Claim 4: Niwamoto + Arling, further in view of Kopf (US 2008/0294667 A1) for HTTP/file-name request teaching.
- Claims 6, 7, 14: Niwamoto + Arling, further in view of Yuh (US 7,093,003 B2) for server GUI/provisioning teaching.

Reasons (concise):
- The specification and claim amendments continue to recite known elements: serving GUI pages to networked personal devices, activatable links, tag files/XML representing device definitions and command lists, selection of pages tailored to device capability, and retrieving/storing GUI and protocol data on local or remote servers. Niwamoto discloses serving GUI pages and link-based interaction between a user device and gateway/gateway-stored resources (specification supporting "causing a graphical user interface page to be provided to the personal communication device"). Arling discloses XML/tag files and associating device information and command elements in tag-like structures (Office action cites Arling ¶30). Kopf and Yuh teach use of HTTP/file-name resource requests and server-based GUI/command provisioning respectively. Combining these teachings would have been an ordinary and predictable design choice for a person having ordinary skill in the art to provide the claimed functionality (per the rationale already stated in the November 2014 action). See the Office action summary (Nov. 3, 2014) for specific mappings of claim elements to the references of record.
- Applicant's arguments that Niwamoto's architecture routes via an adaptor and that adding an executable tag-file capability would 'change the principle' of Niwamoto do not establish nonobviousness. The asserted modification (interpreting/using stored tag/XML data at the gateway or server to form/send appliance-appropriate commands, and using GUI links/file-name-identifiable resources to select those tag files) is a routine architectural option and is supported by the cited references that teach network-served resources, XML/tag data, and HTTP/URI-based requests. The Examiner therefore finds the record combination still presents a prima facie case of obviousness for the claims currently pending.

3) Claim form objections (requires correction)
- Several claims contain unclear antecedent/dependency language likely due to typographical errors in the submitted claim set. Examples: claim 3 reads in the record as "The slave relay station as recited in claim 2 1, wherein..." and claim 7 reads "The slave relay station as recited in claim 7 1, wherein...". Such internal references are indefinite or nonsensical and must be corrected. Provide a corrected claim listing that: (a) uses proper antecedent identifiers (e.g., "The slave relay station as recited in claim 1..." or "The slave relay station as recited in claim 2..."), (b) removes duplicate/malformed dependency numbering, and (c) presents the claims in clean form. The Examiner cannot treat unclear dependencies as allowable language; please submit an amended claim set that fixes these formal defects.

4) Examiner response to applicant remarks
- Applicant argued Arling's XML is merely state data and not an executable tag file that causes direct appliance transmissions. The Examiner notes that Arling describes XML/tag constructs and that interpreting or processing XML-formatted tag data to derive commands is a routine programming step. The Office's combination of references shows the elements claimed—GUI links, resources identifiable by file name or tag reference, XML/tag storage of device/command data, and server/gateway execution or interpretation to format/send appliance commands—are all taught separately and would be combined by a person of ordinary skill for predictable reasons (interoperability, use of known web protocols, flexibility of server-side provisioning). Consequently, the 103 rejections are maintained.
- Applicant's statement reserving right to argue dependent claims is noted. After correction of the claim dependency/form issues, the Examiner will review any argument or amendment specific to particular dependent claims.

5) Next steps / requirements to applicant
- File a corrected set of claims with clean antecedent language and no typographical dependency errors. If applicant wishes to press substantive arguments against the maintained rejections, present (1) persuasive explanation why the combination of references is unsound as a matter of fact or law (for example, pointing to explicit teachings in the references that would teach away from combining), or (2) amendments that clearly set forth limitations not suggested by the cited art. If amendments are made, provide clear support in the specification for any newly added limitations.
- If applicant believes any cited reference has been mischaracterized, specify the exact passages relied upon and explain why the Examiner's characterization is incorrect, with precise record citations.

6) Conclusion / action on record
- The Examiner maintains the rejections under 35 U.S.C. 103 for the pending claims as described above. This non-final action gives applicant an opportunity to submit corrected claim form and/or substantive response addressing the maintained obviousness grounds. Absent appropriate response, the Examiner may continue prosecution which could include an eventual final rejection if the rejections remain unresolved.

Limitations / uncertainties

If applicant submits further evidence or arguments that materially change the evidentiary record, the Examiner will reconsider the findings.

Required formal correction

Examiner contact

parsed.office_action:
DETAILED ACTION

Background
The application is being examined under the pre-AIA first-to-invent provisions. An earlier Office action dated May 8, 2014 (document HUVLV8HBPXXIFW4) placed claims 1–20 under a nonstatutory (obviousness-type) double patenting rejection over claims 1–33 of U.S. Patent No. 9,213,255. Applicant's reply filed August 5, 2014 (A1) includes remarks stating that "A Terminal Disclaimer is submitted herewith" and requests withdrawal of the double-patenting rejection.

Disposition and Reasons for Continued Rejection
Double Patenting (nonstatutory) — maintained (claims 1–20)
Claims 1–20 remain subject to the nonstatutory obviousness-type double patenting rejection over U.S. Patent No. 9,213,255 (claims 1–33) as set forth in the May 8, 2014 Office action. The Office action explained that, although the claims in the instant application are not identical to those of the patent, they are not patentably distinct and thus are unpatentable under double-patenting principles. Applicant's A1 filing requests withdrawal of the rejection and states that "A Terminal Disclaimer is submitted herewith." The examiner has reviewed the application file record available as of the date of this communication and finds no terminal disclaimer document that has been entered in the file wrapper which overcomes the rejection.
Under the Office practice, a nonstatutory double patenting rejection may be overcome by filing a terminal disclaimer in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 1.321 when the required common ownership (or qualifying joint research agreement) condition is met. A terminal disclaimer must be properly signed and must comply with the regulatory requirements. If a terminal disclaimer is not of record, the rejection must be maintained.
Accordingly, the rejection of claims 1–20 over U.S. Patent No. 9,213,255 is continued for the following reason(s):
- The May 8, 2014 Office action made the double patenting ground of rejection of record (HUVLV8HBPXXIFW4: "Claims 1-20 are rejected on the ground of nonstatutory double patenting as being unpatentable over claims 1-33 of U.S. Patent No. 9,213,255.").
- Applicant's August 5, 2014 response (HYHHWFFNPXXIFW3) asserts that a terminal disclaimer was submitted. The examiner finds no terminal disclaimer in the file that has been entered and that meets the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 1.321. The mere statement that a terminal disclaimer was submitted in the reply paper is not sufficient to establish that a compliant terminal disclaimer is of record.

What Applicant Must Do to Overcome the Double Patenting Rejection
To place the application in condition for further consideration with respect to the double patenting rejection, Applicant should take one of the following actions:
1) If a terminal disclaimer was actually submitted via EFS-Web or another filing route but not yet associated with the file, provide documentation that identifies the submission (for example, the EFS confirmation number and the exact submission date/time), and file a copy of the terminal disclaimer (PDF) as a reply paper so that it can be associated with the application record. The terminal disclaimer must meet the formal and substantive requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 1.321, including a proper signature and identification of the patent (U.S. Patent No. 9,213,255) as the patent over which the disclaimer is made. The terminal disclaimer must also comply with the common-ownership or joint-research agreement requirements (37 C.F.R. § 1.321(c) or (d)), or the disclaimer will not be effective to overcome the rejection.
OR
2) If no terminal disclaimer has been filed, file a terminal disclaimer that complies with 37 C.F.R. § 1.321. The terminal disclaimer must: (a) identify U.S. Patent No. 9,213,255 as the patent over which the disclaimer is made; (b) be signed in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 1.321(b) by a person authorized to sign; and (c) include the statement of common ownership or show that the statutory joint research agreement exception applies (37 C.F.R. § 1.321(c) or (d)). If the terminal disclaimer meets the requirements, and is entered into the file, the double patenting rejection will be reconsidered in view of the entered terminal disclaimer.
OR
3) If the double patenting rejection is to be opposed on the ground that claims are patentably distinct, submit persuasive argument and, where appropriate, claim amendments and evidence demonstrating patentable distinction over the claims of U.S. Patent No. 9,213,255. Note that absent an entered terminal disclaimer, argument alone must persuasively show patentable distinction over the identified patent claims.

If Applicant files a terminal disclaimer meeting the statutory and regulatory requirements and it is entered in the file, the examiner will withdraw the nonstatutory double patenting rejection as to the claims covered by the terminal disclaimer, subject to any other outstanding substantive rejections or formal objections.

Timing and Procedural Matters
- If Applicant intends to rely on a terminal disclaimer that is already filed but not yet of record, identifying the submission (EFS confirmation number and submission timestamp) and providing a copy of the filed terminal disclaimer as a reply paper will expedite correction of the file and reconsideration of the rejection. Failure to provide an entered terminal disclaimer or other appropriate response will result in maintenance of the double patenting rejection and further action.
- The applicant's August 5, 2014 claim set has been noted and will be treated as the pending claims. This Office action is limited to the double patenting issue described above. Any other outstanding examination matters remain unaffected and may be addressed in subsequent communications if present.

Conclusion and Next Steps
The double patenting rejection of claims 1–20 is continued because there is no terminal disclaimer of record that overcomes the rejection. Applicant should either (A) submit a compliant terminal disclaimer that identifies U.S. Patent No. 9,213,255 and meets the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 1.321 (and ensure it is entered into the file), or (B) provide documentary evidence that satisfies the common-ownership or joint-research agreement requirement, or (C) present persuasive argument and/or claim amendments demonstrating patentable distinction from the cited patent claims.

The examiner is available for telephone conference if Applicant wishes to discuss the specific requirements for a terminal disclaimer or evidence appropriate to show common ownership. If Applicant has already filed the terminal disclaimer, please identify the EFS confirmation and provide a copy so this office can correct the file and withdraw the double patenting rejection upon entry of a compliant terminal disclaimer.

(Administrative note) The examiner's prior guidance in the May 8, 2014 communication (HUVLV8HBPXXIFW4) and the present action should be read together. The May 8, 2014 action set forth the double patenting grounds; Applicant's reply asserts a terminal disclaimer but no terminal disclaimer document is of record. The present action explains what is required to place the application in condition for allowance with respect to the double patenting ground.

Limitations
- The record available to the examiner does not include a terminal disclaimer document that has been entered in the application file wrapper. If the applicant can show by documentary evidence that a compliant terminal disclaimer has in fact been filed and entered, this communication will be superseded accordingly. The examiner does not decline to recognize a terminal disclaimer that was in fact filed; rather, the examiner must act on what is of record.
- The examiner has not performed an independent reexamination of the entire scope of claims 1–20 against U.S. Patent No. 9,213,255 beyond the double patenting concern previously made of record. The double patenting rejection is maintained solely because it is not yet overcome by an entered terminal disclaimer or other appropriate evidence or argument.

If Applicant elects to file a terminal disclaimer, please ensure that the terminal disclaimer (1) explicitly identifies U.S. Patent No. 9,213,255 as the patent over which the terminal disclaimer is made, (2) includes a statement that the terminal disclaimer is being filed to obviate the nonstatutory double patenting rejection with respect to the identified patent, and (3) otherwise complies with 37 C.F.R. § 1.321 in form and signature. If Applicant believes a terminal disclaimer was already filed, identify the EFS confirmation number and submit a copy so the file can be corrected and the rejection reconsidered.
