Decision on Applicant's A1 submission and next steps
Summary
- Applicant has canceled the originally-filed claims 1–12 and filed a new claim set numbered 13–24 (doc IK8LKB0DPXXIFW1). The cancellation of claims 1–12 makes prior objections and rejections that were directed solely to those canceled claims moot. The record reflects that specification and drawing amendments were submitted and replacement drawing sheets were filed (docs IK8LKAZQPXXIFW1 and IK8LKB0PPXXIFW1). These drawing and specification amendments are noted and have been entered for consideration.
- The new independent claim is claim 13. Claims 14–24 depend directly or indirectly from claim 13. The newly presented claims will now be examined on the merits under the statutes and rules applicable to the application.
Entered/withdrawn claim matters
- Withdrawn: Original claims 1–12 are canceled by Applicant and therefore withdrawn. The examiner will not issue further rejections addressed specifically to those canceled claims. (Support: IK8LKB0DPXXIFW1 "1.-12. (Canceled)").
- Entered: The examiner has entered Applicant's new claims 13–24 for examination. (Support: IK8LKB0DPXXIFW1, claim text beginning at "13. (New) An apparatus for dental floss, comprising:").
Preliminary examiner position on new claims (13–24)
- Claim 13 recites (in pertinent part) an elongate holding element with a bore running substantially along its length; a floss string with enlarged ends larger than the bore diameter; and a frangible section so the elongate element can be broken into two parts and pulled apart along the floss until the floss ends abut the bore ends, "whereby the floss string slides lengthwise through the bore of at least one of the two parts when the two parts are pulled apart." Applicant argues (in the A1 response) that the prior art of record does not teach the latter sliding limitation. The examiner acknowledges Applicant's argument and will now analyze claim 13 and its dependents in view of the entire prior art record (including Hovel, Court, Charatan, Berglund, and Lorch which were made of record in the September 2, 2015 Office action IDZX5FZ9PXXIFW4). The examiner will determine whether the claimed combination of structural features (bore, enlarged floss ends, frangible element, and sliding of the floss in the bore during separation) is either taught or rendered obvious by the prior art of record.
- At this time the examiner cannot accept Applicant's conclusory statement that "the prior art of record fails to disclose" the claimed sliding limitation without providing a substantive showing that the combination of structural elements is not disclosed or suggested by the references of record. The earlier Office action set forth specific references and rationales that will be considered against the new claims. For example, the prior Office action cited Court and Hovel as teaching paper sheets rolled about floss and other references for handle dimensions and frangible constructs. Those references remain in the file and will be considered in light of the new claim language.
Planned next substantive action
- Non-final action on the merits (this communication): The examiner issues this Non-Final examination communication to (1) confirm entry of the new claims, (2) advise Applicant that claims 1–12 are canceled and prior rejections to those claims are moot, and (3) notify Applicant that claim 13 (and dependents) will be examined for patentability in light of the prior art of record and the specification as amended. The examiner will complete the examination of claims 13–24 and will either: (a) allow the claims if they are found to be patentable as amended and supported by the specification, or (b) issue one or more rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102, 103, and/or 112 with a reasoned explanation referencing the specific prior art where applicable. The examiner will also check that the amended drawings and specification comply with the formal requirements noted in the prior Office action and that the drawings objections previously raised (solid black shading, view numbers) have been overcome by the replacement sheets.
Issues the examiner will address in the next action (non-exhaustive)
1) 35 U.S.C. 112(a) / written description and enablement — The examiner will verify that each limitation of claims 13–24 is supported in the specification as originally filed or as properly amended (the specification changes entered must not introduce new matter). If support is lacking for a particular limitation (for instance, a very specific structural/functional interaction or an exact dimension not supported), the examiner will identify the deficiency. Applicant's remarks point to figures and specification passages for support; the examiner will cite the specific support or identify any deficiency.
2) 35 U.S.C. 112(b) / clarity and proper antecedent basis — The examiner will construe claim 13 and its dependents and will identify any clarity problems (e.g., if terms such as "frangible section," "slides lengthwise," "first diameter/second diameter" lack clear antecedent basis or are otherwise indefinite). If claim constructions or amendments are required for clarity, the examiner will specify the problematic language and propose (or request) corrective amendment(s).
3) 35 U.S.C. 102/103 — The examiner will determine whether the claimed arrangement (including the dynamic limitation that the floss slides lengthwise through the bore of at least one part during separation) is taught or would have been obvious over the prior art of record (Hovel, Court, Charatan, Berglund, Lorch, etc.) or over any other references found in the prior art search. If a rejection is made, the examiner will explain with particularity how the references teach or render obvious each claim limitation and why a person of ordinary skill would combine the teachings.
Formalities and entered amendments
- The amendment to the specification and the replacement drawings have been received and entered. The examiner will review the replacement drawings for compliance with 37 C.F.R. 1.84 and 1.121. Applicant's remarks represent belief that the prior drawing objections have been overcome; the examiner will either withdraw the drawing objections if compliance is confirmed or identify any remaining drawing formalities.
Opportunity for interview and response
- Applicant is invited to request an examiner interview to discuss claim construction, the particular interpretation of the dynamic "slides lengthwise" limitation, or to present further evidence or amendments to overcome any forthcoming rejection. An interview may facilitate advance resolution and may avoid an unnecessary additional Office action.
Timing and further action
- Within the next Office action the examiner will either (a) allow one or more claims if patentable or (b) set forth rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102, 103, and/or 112 with accompanying rationale. Applicant will then have the normal statutory time period to respond.
Concluding note
- The record shows Applicant's belief that the new claims are patentable over the prior art. The examiner will perform a reasoned analysis of the newly entered independent claim and dependents and will communicate the result in the next substantive Office action. If Applicant wishes to expedite resolution, consider (i) providing a claim chart mapping claim limitations to specific passages in the specification, and/or (ii) requesting an interview to explain how the structural and functional interplay in claim 13 distinguishes over each applied reference.

Applicant's A1 traversal argues that the amended claim 6 requires (inter alia) that (i) the groove be in a light‑shielding region and (ii) the liquid crystal layer at the groove position has thickness substantially equal to or larger than the liquid crystal layer in an active area which is not shielded from light — and that Choi's disclosed contact hole/groove has a thickness smaller than the active area, so Choi does not anticipate. Applicant asserts that Andrews does not cure Choi's deficiency for the combination claim 7 objection. These are substantive arguments; the Examiner will address them once the Applicant's amended claim text is entered for examination. At this time:
  - The record (O1) shows the Office applied Choi to the then‑of‑record claims and considered Choi's contact hole/groove to correspond to the claimed groove/contact hole and Choi's polymer/PS teaching to correspond to the claimed polymer layer. The Examiner relied on Choi's disclosures (as summarized in O1) to reject claims 6, 8 and 9 under 102. The Examiner will re-open consideration of those rejections and will either withdraw or maintain them after entry of the A1 amendment and re‑analysis of Choi against the entered claim language.
  - For claim 7, the Examiner's prior reasoning that Andrews teaches small photospacer diameters and that it would have been obvious to apply such sizes to the arrangement in Choi remains the articulated basis for the 103 rejection (see O1). Applicant's assertion that there would be no motivation or reason to modify Choi must be supported by specific record evidence (for example, a teaching‑away passage in Choi or Andrews, experimental data, or claim limitations added by amendment that distinguish over the cited combination). Broad statements that the combination is improper are insufficient.
Required Applicant Actions and Next Steps
1) Entry confirmation: If Applicant's October 17, 2016 amendment (A1) is intended to be entered and considered now, identify the exact transaction that caused entry in the Office record (for example, confirm the replacement drawing sheet was accepted and the claims were entered). If entry has not yet occurred, Applicant should file a corrected replacement drawing sheet(s) and/or claim/specification amendments explicitly complying with 37 CFR 1.121 and 1.84 as necessary, and request entry. If Applicant requests entry, include redlined (if possible) or a clear indication of the changes and the complete set of amended claims intended to be of record. The Examiner will not withdraw the outstanding rejections until the amendment is of record and examined.
2) For the 112(b) rejection: After entry, the Examiner will decide whether the prior 112 objections are resolved. If Applicant believes the 112 objections were fully resolved by the October 17, 2016 amendments, provide a short statement pointing to the exact places in the amended specification or drawings that supply antecedent basis for the previously‑called-out phrases (cite paragraph numbers and figure numbers/labels from the entered material). If the Examiner still finds indefiniteness, a new 112 rejection or an explanation of remaining defects will be issued.
3) For the 102 and 103 rejections: After entry, the Examiner will re-evaluate Choi and Andrews against the entered claims. If Applicant relies on the position that Choi does not disclose the relative-thickness limitation, Applicant must identify where in Choi (by figure and paragraph) Choi allegedly discloses a contrary relationship (i.e., show that Choi's groove/contact-hole region has LC thickness smaller than active area) or otherwise provide evidence to support non-anticipation or non-obviousness. If Applicant has experimental evidence or other objective evidence to rebut the Examiner's prima facie case of anticipation or obviousness, submit it now.
4) If Applicant maintains traversal of the restriction requirement (Group II election was made on record earlier), the Applicant may file a divisional application to pursue the non-elected Group I claims (Applicant stated a reservation to file a divisional). That is procedural and does not affect the present prosecution of Group II claims.
Conclusion / Action Requested
- The Examiner maintains the outstanding rejections from the July 22, 2016 Office action (112(b) for claims 6–9 and 102/103 rejections as set forth). Applicant's October 17, 2016 amendment and arguments have been noted. To proceed, Applicant must ensure the 10/17/2016 amendment is entered; and, to the extent Applicant requests withdrawal of any rejection, Applicant should point to the exact passages in the now‑entered specification/drawings that cure the earlier-cited defects or provide specific record evidence that distinguishes Choi and Andrews from the entered claims. After entry, the Examiner will re-evaluate and issue a subsequent Office action withdrawing or maintaining the cited rejections with written explanation.
- If Applicant intends to have the October 17, 2016 amendment enter the record, please promptly confirm entry or re-submit the corrected replacement drawing sheet(s) and claims per the requirements listed above. If Applicant instead files further amendment or arguments, please ensure they address the specific issues identified in this communication.
Limitations
- The Examiner relied on the application file contents as of the USPTO cutoff date. The A1 (10/17/2016) paper is of record but the Amendment must be entered for substantive examination; this action does not presume the Amendment was entered. If the A1 amendment was entered after the cutoff, notify the Examiner and provide PAIR confirmation so the Examiner may re-evaluate prior rejections against the entered claim set.
- The Examiner's earlier characterization of Choi and Andrews appears in the 7/22/2016 action. A citation to the full text of those references was used in the prior action; Applicant is encouraged to cite specific portions of the cited references if arguing non-anticipation or lack of motivation to combine.
Any inquiry concerning this communication or earlier communications from the examiner should be directed to the primary examiner named in the file.
limitations: Applicant's 2016-10-17 amendments are recorded in the file wrapper but their formal entry for examination is not confirmed as of the cutoff; the Examiner cannot withdraw prior rejections until amendments are entered and examined.

The Examiner's prior rejections relied on the examiner's summarization of Choi and Andrews in the 7/22/2016 action (IQUUZV68RXEAPX5); full-text passages of those foreign/third-party references are not included among the provided input documents, so the Examiner's characterization in O1 is used as record evidence.

If Applicant submits additional evidence (for example, specific citations to Choi or Andrews or experimental data), that evidence must be in the file for the Examiner to consider it in evaluating novelty or obviousness.

applicant_argument_responses.response:
The amendments are acknowledged. However, the amendments do not resolve all of the indefiniteness issues identified in the June 3, 2015 Office action. Examples: (1) Claim 27 now recites "a hydraulic machine with hydraulics" and "an armhydraulic elevator arms attached to the hydraulic machine" — these phrases are grammatically and conceptually unclear and do not provide proper antecedent basis for "the hydraulic machine" or for the elevator arms. (2) Claim 28 contains run-on wording and multiple references to "lower" and "upper" column modules without clearly establishing these as antecedents in claim 27 in its current amended form. (3) Claim 30 recites "thean opening and closing mechanism" and mixes phrasing ("uppertop end column module/unit") that prevents a clear metes-and-bounds construction. (4) Several claims use slashes (e.g., "square and/or cylindrical", "lower and upper column modules") and inconsistent article usage that create ambiguity about whether alternatives or conjunctive limitations are intended. (5) The gateway limitation in claim 27(d) remains internally inconsistent: the clause beginning with a semicolon and "which is moveable..." is grammatically disconnected and includes overlapping descriptive language ("the gateway support structure; which is moveable... the gateway structure comprising...").
Therefore the 35 U.S.C. 112(b) rejection is maintained for the reasons above and as previously set forth in the June 3, 2015 action. To expedite prosecution, the examiner provides suggested corrective guidance below under "Required Applicant Action."

  "office_action": "Examiner's Continued Non‑Final Action\nIntroduction and procedural status\nClaims 1–7 were previously examined and rejected in the Office action mailed June 30, 2016 (Document: IPZEMCDQRXEAPX1). On December 28, 2016 the Applicant filed an amendment and response (A1 documents: IX97YV28RXEAPX5, IX97YV2ARXEAPX5, IX97YV2BRXEAPX5). The Examiner has considered the amendments and the remarks. This communication continues examination and addresses the outstanding rejections and the Applicant's remarks.\nSummary of Examiner determinations\n- Non‑statutory double patenting (dp): The Examiner previously asserted a double patenting ground over U.S. Patent No. 8,639,947 B2. Applicant submitted a Terminal Disclaimer (see IX97YV2BRXEAPX5: 'The Applicant hereby submits a Terminal Disclaimer.'). Upon submission of the terminal disclaimer, the Examiner withdraws the double patenting objection, contingent on entry of the terminal disclaimer into the application record and compliance with 37 C.F.R. 1.321. If the terminal disclaimer is not entered for any procedural reason, the Examiner will reinstate the double patenting ground. No further response on this point is required unless the Applicant is notified that the terminal disclaimer was not entered.\n- 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (indefiniteness): The June 30, 2016 Office action raised 112(b) rejections for claims 1–7. The amendment to independent claim 1 clarifies placement of the encryption module by reciting placing the dedicated encryption module in a DBMS layer that is above the database cache and stating the module is transparent to the application layer. This amendment addresses the Examiner's previous concern about the vagueness of 'above a database cache' insofar as claim 1 now specifies the module sits in a layer of a layered application architecture and is transparent to the application layer. However, the Examiner finds that dependent claim 2 (and thus claims 3–4 which depend from it) as submitted in the A1 response contains garbled and unclear language in the currently‑entered amendment (for example, the phrase 'asumethe-extenee an-l--denEll-idener-that' appears in the current file). Because the claim text is corrupted/ambiguous, the Examiner cannot determine the scope of the limitation reciting the internal cell identifier or how it is 'assumed' in the claim. Under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) claims must particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter; therefore the 112(b) rejection is maintained for claims 2–4. The 112(b) rejection for claim 1 is withdrawn to the extent that claim 1's amendment cures the previously identified indefiniteness; claims 5–7 depend from claim 1 and are therefore not objected to under 112(b) on the prior 'above cache' basis. Action required: Applicant must file clear, non‑corrupted replacement text for claims 2–4 (an amendment that properly and unambiguously recites the intended limitation such as Enc_k(Vtrc)=Ek(μ(t,r,c)⊕Vtrc) or Enc_k(Vtrc)=Ek(μ(t,r,c)∥Vtrc) and a clear textual recitation of the 'internal cell identifier' concept). Once clear claim text is of record, the Examiner will re‑evaluate definiteness and support.\n- 35 U.S.C. 101 (subject matter eligibility): The Examiner has reconsidered Applicant's arguments in the A1 response that claim 1 recites a specific architecture (module placed above cache, transparent to application layer) which supplies an inventive concept. The Examiner acknowledges the added location limitation in claim 1. Nevertheless, claim 1 as amended continues to recite high‑level functional concepts (placing an encryption module in a particular layer of a layered architecture and encrypting values together with coordinates) and mathematical/data‑manipulation activity (encryption and combining data). Under Alice/Mayo framework, the first step requires determining whether the claims are directed to an abstract idea. The Examiner finds the claims are directed to the abstract concept of encrypting information and associating data with coordinates (which includes mathematical manipulation). Under the second step, the Examiner finds that the present claim language does not supply additional inventive features that transform the abstract idea into a patent‑eligible application. The recitation that a module is 'above a database cache' and 'transparent to the application layer' describes a placement and high‑level result but lacks structural and functional detail demonstrating a concrete technological improvement in how the DBMS operates (for example, no specific altered data paths, memory management techniques, or novel internal DBMS control flow are claimed). Therefore the 101 rejection is maintained for claim 1 and dependent claims that do not add further qualifying limitations (claims 5–7). Applicant's arguments about practical advantages and performance are noted; to overcome the 101 rejection Applicant may either amend the claims to include specific technical implementation details showing improved computer functioning, or submit persuasive technical evidence tying claimed features to concrete improvements in computer operation.\n- 35 U.S.C. 103 (obviousness): Claims 1 and claims 5–7 remain rejected as obvious over Sutter (US 6,446,092 B1) in view of Damiani et al. (Balancing Confidentiality and Efficiency in Untrusted Relational DBMSs), for the reasons described in the June 30, 2016 Office action and summarized therein. The Examiner has considered Applicant's traversal distinguishing the cited references (e.g., Sutter's focus on application‑layer encryption for replication/security and Damiani's tuple/column teachings). The Examiner finds that Sutter and Damiani teach related goals and techniques (encryption of database content, use of per‑location or per‑column auxiliary data, index-related handling) and that a skilled artisan would have had reason to combine these teachings to bind encrypted values to a database location and to support index/backup behavior. The 103 rejection is therefore maintained for claims 1 and 5–7. To traverse this rejection, Applicant may (a) amend claims to add limitations not taught or suggested by the cited art (for example, a particular non‑conventional mechanism for generating/protecting the internal cell identifier or a particular session key‑management technique that is not disclosed in the cited art), or (b) present objective evidence (e.g., comparative technical results) showing unexpected advantages not suggested by the prior art combination.\nDetailed points and guidance\n1) Terminal disclaimer: The Applicant's submission of a Terminal Disclaimer in the A1 remarks (IX97YV2BRXEAPX5) is noted. The Examiner has withdrawn the double patenting objection contingent upon entry of an appropriate disclaimer. If the disclaimer is not entered for any reason, the Examiner will notify Applicant and will reinstate the double patenting ground. No additional reply on this issue is required unless Applicant is informed the disclaimer was not entered.\n2) Claims 2–4: The file record contains corrupted/ambiguous claim language for these dependent claims in the A1 submission. Applicant must file an amendment that replaces the garbled text with clear, unambiguous language. The Examiner suggests copying verbatim the intended formula and definitions from the specification (for example, Enc_k(Vtrc)=Ek(μ(t,r,c)⊕Vtrc) and a clear recitation of μ and the internal cell identifier), and ensuring the amendment is submitted in a format accepted by the Office (clean, machine‑readable text) so that the Office record properly reflects the proposed wording. Until the corrected claim text is entered, the 112(b) rejection for claims 2–4 will be maintained.\n3) 35 U.S.C. 101: If Applicant wishes the Examiner to reconsider eligibility, Applicant should either: (a) amend the claims to recite specific, concrete technical features that demonstrate an improvement to computer or DBMS functioning (for example, specific modifications to cache read/write hooks, precise in‑process key handling, particular cryptographic binding routines implemented at defined software points), or (b) submit evidence (benchmarks, technical data) showing the claimed arrangement produces a specific technical improvement attributable to claimed structural/functional features. Broad high‑level result statements and advantages, without tying them to concrete claimed structure/steps, are insufficient to overcome the 101 rejection under Alice step two.\n4) 35 U.S.C. 103: To overcome the obviousness rejection, Applicant may amend claims to include features absent from the cited art and which are not obvious from the combination, or supply objective evidence (e.g., unexpected results, long‑felt need, commercial success attributable to the claimed features) that supports nonobviousness.\nConclusion and required Applicant action\n1) The non‑statutory double patenting rejection is withdrawn contingent on entry of the Terminal Disclaimer that Applicant submitted. No further action is required unless the Office later advises that the disclaimer was not entered.\n2) The 35 U.S.C. 112(b) rejection is withdrawn for claim 1 but is maintained for claims 2–4 due to corrupted/indefinite wording in the recorded amendment. Applicant must file corrected, unambiguous claim text for claims 2–4. Provide clean amended claim text with clear formulae and definitions (e.g., exact Enc/Dec formulas and a clear definition of μ and 'internal cell identifier').\n3) The 35 U.S.C. 101 rejection is maintained for claim 1 and dependent claims that do not add qualifying limitations (claims 5–7). Applicant may respond by amendment to add concrete structural/functional limitations that show an improvement in DBMS functioning or by submitting persuasive technical evidence tied to the claimed features.\n4) The 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection is maintained for claims 1 and 5–7 over Sutter in view of Damiani et al. Applicant may amend claims to include non‑obvious features or submit objective evidence of nonobviousness.\n5) After Applicant files corrected claims 2–4 and any substantive reply (amendment or evidence) addressing the 101 and/or 103 issues, the Examiner will reconsider and will take further action (possible allowance, or further amendment/rejection) as appropriate.\nLimitations and procedural notes\n- The Examiner acted based on the record documents available through the stated cutoff. The Terminal Disclaimer was identified in the A1 remarks and the Examiner acted consistent with its submission; actual entry into the file will be verified by the Office electronic record. If the Terminal Disclaimer is not entered, the double patenting ground may be reinstated.\n- Claim 2's amendment as filed in the A1 appears to contain corrupted text. The Examiner cannot treat corrupted text as a definitive amendment; a corrected clean replacement is required.\nExaminer contact\nIf the Applicant wishes to discuss this action prior to filing a response, the Examiner can be contacted via the mechanisms shown in the file record.",

ACTION ON APPLICANT'S APRIL 5, 2016 SUBMISSION
Status summary
- Claims 1 and 2: maintained as allowable for reasons stated in the January 5, 2016 Office action. Applicant's amendment to claims 1 and 2 is recognized; no further substantive objection is made for patentability over the record prior art relied on to date. Proceed with allowance formalities after applicant addresses processing and formality matters as noted below. 
- Claim 3: the 35 U.S.C. § 103 rejection over Edmond (US 5,539,217) is maintained. Applicant's traversal has been considered but does not, without additional evidence, overcome the prima facie case of obviousness.
Discussion and reasons for action
1) Claims 1–2 (method claims) The Examiner's prior statement that claims 1 and 2 are allowable stands. The record in the Office action (Jan. 5, 2016) explains that the particular temperature-gradient relationship (formula (1)) recited in claim 1 is not taught or suggested by the prior art of record. Applicant has submitted amended claim text for claims 1–2 (A1 amendment). No persuasive evidence or argument in the A1 contradicts the examiner's prior determination of allowability for these claims. Therefore claims 1 and 2 remain allowable. Applicant is advised to submit a clean corrected copy of the allowed claim set and to complete any outstanding formalities (e.g., any necessary drawing corrections, inventor or attorney signatures, or payment of the issue fee and publication/printing fees) to proceed toward allowance. If applicant intends to further amend any allowed claims, note that such amendments could reopen examination.
Supporting record excerpts:
- "Claims 1-2 are allowed prior art of record." (Jan. 5, 2016 Office Action)
- As filed claim language defining the temperature-gradient formula (formula (1)) and ranges appears at ID99A9HOPXXIFW3 (claims).
2) Claim 3 (product claim) — 35 U.S.C. § 103 (maintained)
Ground and examiner analysis: Claim 3 recites "A p-type SiC single crystal containing no inclusions and having resistivity of 35 to 120 mΩ·cm." The prior Office action (Jan. 5, 2016) rejected claim 3 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Edmond (US 5,539,217). The Examiner relied on Edmond's disclosure of a p-type SiC substrate and discussed that Edmond's resistivity figures (as cited in the action) overlap the claimed resistivity range. The Examiner also cited the well-established legal principle that selecting a workable range within a broader prior-art disclosure is prima facie obvious absent a showing of criticality or unexpected properties; the specification in this application does not provide the evidence of criticality required to rebut that presumption.
Applicant's arguments in A1 and Examiner response:
- Applicant argument: Applicant contends Edmond's statement that substrate 11 "contains no n-type dopant" is not equivalent to the present claim language "containing no inclusions," and argues that the claimed crystal free of inclusions and having the recited low resistivity was first obtained by the present invention. Applicant asserts that a person of ordinary skill would have assumed a p-type SiC single crystal could not both be free of inclusions and have resistivity 35–120 mΩ·cm based on Edmond and other art.
- Examiner response: The Examiner acknowledges the semantic distinction applicant makes between "n-type dopant" and "inclusions." However, that semantic distinction does not, without corroborating evidentiary support, rebut the legal principle applied in the prior Office action: where the prior art discloses conditions that overlap a claimed range, selection of a sub-range is prima facie obvious unless applicant shows that the claimed range is critical, yields unexpected properties, or that the cited prior art would not have suggested the claimed combination. The Examiner points to the O1 text: "With reference to Fig. 1, Edmond teaches a p-type SiC single crystal 11 containing no inclusions (interpreted as containing no n-type dopant) and having resistivity of 100 to 200 mΩ.cm (col. 5, lines 35-36)." The Examiner also cited the legal authorities regarding range selection and the need for a showing of criticality or unexpected results (In re Aller, In re Kulling, etc.). Applicant's remarks do not include experimental data, declarations, or documentary evidence that establish the claimed resistivity range is critical or that the absence of inclusions in the claimed crystals is an unexpected property that would not have been arrived at by routine experimentation.
What is required to overcome the rejection of claim 3:
- If applicant wishes to overcome the rejection of claim 3, applicant should file one or more of the following: (a) evidence (e.g., declarations by inventors or qualified practitioners, experimental data, comparative tables) demonstrating that: (i) the claimed resistivity range (35–120 mΩ·cm) produces unexpected results compared to the closest prior art (for example, improvements in inclusion absence, crystal quality, device performance attributable to the claimed range), or (ii) the claimed combination of "no inclusions" and the recited resistivity is not disclosed or suggested by Edmond and cannot be obtained by routine optimization; or (b) proposed claim amendments that carve out a patentable distinction from Edmond supported by the specification. Declarations or data should be specific and show why the claimed range is critical and not the result of routine optimization. Broad conclusory statements are not sufficient. If applicant can point to particular passages in Edmond that do or do not teach the alleged features, supply specific citations and, if available, copies of relevant Edmond passages (if not already of record).
Procedural disposition and next steps
- The 35 U.S.C. § 103 rejection of claim 3 is maintained. The application remains with at least one outstanding rejection (claim 3). Therefore a final allowance/patent grant cannot be completed until the outstanding rejection is resolved. This communication is a non-final action continuing prosecution (CTFR). Applicant may respond to this action by either: (1) submitting persuasive evidence or amendments that overcome the rejection of claim 3, or (2) filing a request for continued examination (RCE) if appropriate, or (3) electing to cancel claim 3 and proceed to allowance of the remaining claims (1–2) by completing allowance formalities.
- If applicant cancels claim 3 in a reply and completes the issue/allowance formalities for claims 1–2, the Examiner will process the application toward allowance for the remaining claims in accordance with the prior allowance statement.
Limitations / uncertainties
- The Examiner relies on the record of Edmond as cited in the January 5, 2016 Office action; the Examiner has not independently reproduced Edmond's experimental data. If applicant contends Edmond does not disclose any of the relied-upon features, applicant should point to the specific Edmond passages or submit a copy of Edmond with highlighted text to show the alleged difference.
- Applicant's statement that the invention was the first to obtain a low-resistance p-type SiC single crystal containing no inclusions is a factual assertion that requires supporting evidence (declarations, experimental data). The specification as filed does not supply data showing that the claimed resistivity range is critical or yields unexpected results sufficient to overcome the prima facie case of obviousness applied to claim 3.
Concluding remark
Applicant is invited to respond within the statutory time period for reply to this non-final action. If applicant submits evidence or amendments, the Examiner will consider them and either withdraw the rejection if appropriate or maintain/confirm the rejection with further explanation. If applicant elects to cancel claim 3 and proceed to allowance of claims 1–2, the Examiner will continue processing allowance formalities upon receipt of all required documents and fees.

Examiner Notice — Continued Non-Final Action (Substantive Response to Applicant A1)
Summary of Procedural Posture
- The application has a prior Office action dated 07/22/2016 (IQV0V978RXEAPX0) rejecting claims 1–15 under 35 U.S.C. 103 over Leech in view of Forest, and rejecting claims 16–20 under 35 U.S.C. 103 over Leech in view of Forest and Savarese. That Office action is of record and formed the basis for the applicant's A1 response filed 10/24/2016 (IUOMUKBVRXEAPX1, IUOMUKBWRXEAPX1).
- Applicant filed amended claims (claims 1, 2, 12, 16, 19) and new claim 21, cancelled claim 18, and made arguments. The amendments appear as proposed claims in the file wrapper (entry status for those amendments is recorded as 'unknown' in the prosecution snapshot). This communication responds to applicant's arguments and the amendments recorded in the A1 paper.
Status of Rejections
- The Examiner maintains the previously stated 35 U.S.C. 103 rejections as outstanding for the claims listed in the July 22, 2016 Office action. Specifically, claims 1–15 remain rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 over Leech in view of Forest, and claims 16, 17, 19, 20 remain rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 over Leech in view of Forest and Savarese. The rejections are maintained for the following reasons summarized below.
Response to Applicant's Arguments and Amendments
1) Applicant's substantive argument: Leech and Forest do not teach using computerized eyewear to record an orientation of a golf player relative to the ball as the player executes a shot; therefore the Examiner should withdraw the 103 rejection of claim 1.
Examiner response: The prior action identified Leech as teaching wearable eyewear with display and ball-tracking capabilities and identified Forest as teaching use of course and player data, recommendations, and graphical summaries. Applicant's amendment to claim 1 now recites that, "as the particular golf player is playing the particular hole ... using a set of computerized eyewear to record play information including a location of each stroke ... and an orientation of the particular golf player relative to a golf ball ... as the particular player is executing the particular shot." The amendment thus places emphasis on orientation-recording by the eyewear during execution of a shot. Applicant's argument states that neither Leech nor Forest teach such orientation-recording; however, the record as it stands contains the prior office action's characterizations of the cited references but does not contain the full text passages of Leech and Forest that are needed in the record to conclusively support applicant's factual assertion of non-teaching. In view of the prior rejection and the cited combination, and absent submitted textual passages or other persuasive evidence from the applicant that establish non-disclosure in the cited references, the Examiner must treat the rejections as still supported for the present prosecution stage. If applicant believes particular cited passages in Leech or Forest do not disclose the claimed orientation-recording limitation, applicant should specifically point to those passages (by paragraph and/or figure) and explain the differences, or submit an affidavit or declaration under 37 C.F.R. § 1.132 setting forth evidence of non-disclosure (for example, a side-by-side comparison or expert statement). Alternatively, applicant may amend claims to recite specific sensor hardware, sensor placement, or particular data processing steps (for example, specifying a head-worn IMU and a defined sensor-fusion algorithm) not suggested by the cited references.
2) Applicant's argument regarding motivation to combine: Applicant contends Leech addresses ball tracking after a shot and Forest addresses coaching prior to a shot; they are unrelated problems and there is no motivation to combine.
Examiner response: The prior office action set forth a rationale for combination — namely that Leech teaches eyewear and display/ball tracking and Forest teaches deriving recommendations and using course/player data to recommend actions; a person of ordinary skill could be motivated to combine wearable eyewear that presents advice based on course and player data. The applicant's argument is primarily an assertion of lack of motivation. To rebut a prima facie case of obviousness, applicant should provide evidence of secondary considerations (objective indicia) such as unexpected results, commercial success tied to the claimed features, long-felt but unsolved need, or failure of others, or show that the cited combination would destroy a critical teaching or operate in a fundamentally incompatible manner. Mere attorney argument that the references solve different problems is not sufficient when the references address related technical fields (golf-related eyewear, player/course data, and coaching functions). The applicant may also narrow claims to recite specific structural or procedural limitations that are not suggested by the prior art combination.
3) Applicant's arguments about Figures 21–23 and Figure 9 of Forest: Applicant contends these do not teach using player's own past play data to determine aim or generating the claimed visual hole summary with player orientations.
Examiner response: If applicant asserts that Forest does not disclose specific features, applicant must identify where Forest does or does not disclose the claimed elements with record citations. The Examiner relied on Forest for teachings regarding use of course/player data and visual summaries; to the extent applicant contends Forest lacks the particular feature, applicant must show the absence with evidence or amend to further distinguish. As before, citation of precise passages or submission of an admissible declaration is helpful.
Claim 21 (new): This claim recites that the eyewear comprises a GPS sensor and one or more accelerometers and that orientation-recording is performed using those sensors.
Examiner response: Claim 21 narrows claim 1 by adding specific sensors. If applicant wishes to rely upon claim 21 as a distinguishing limitation, applicant should: (1) clearly support the specific sensor-based limitation in the specification (the specification includes mention of GPS and accelerometers — see SPEC pgpub_description and figures discussing GPS and accelerometers and recording orientation — ensure support), and (2) address whether the cited references teach the claimed sensor combination. If Leech, Forest, or Savarese disclose GPS and accelerometers in wearable eyewear (or teach combining such sensors with wearable displays), claim 21 may still be unpatentable as obvious; applicant should point out any absence in the cited references with documentary support. The Examiner notes that the specification as filed mentions GPS and accelerometers among sensors (see pgpub_description and SPEC record), which provides written support for claim 21, but whether those sensors render claim 21 nonobvious depends upon the cited art. Applicant should submit precise reference citations or further claim amendment if the sensor combination is not taught by the references.
Typographical/Claim-Form Matters
- The Examiner notes typographical errors in the amended claim language (e.g., "evewear", "athe", duplicate articles). Applicant should correct these typographical/grammatical errors in any future claim amendment to avoid potential clarity issues under 37 CFR 1.75(d). If the applicant intends different wording, please amend accordingly.
Action To Applicant / Required Response
- The Examiner maintains the 103 rejections as outstanding. Applicant is encouraged to: (A) provide specific, pinpoint citations (figure/paragraph/column) from Leech, Forest, and Savarese (or other references) if applicant disputes the Examiner's characterization of the prior art; (B) supply admissible evidence (e.g., declaration under 37 C.F.R. § 1.132 or evidence of secondary considerations) showing non-obviousness; or (C) amend claims to include additional structural or functional limitations that are supported by the specification and that clearly distinguish the claims from the applied art (for example, detail particular sensor placements, sensor fusion algorithms, timing of orientation capture tied to execution of the shot, or other inventive steps). If applicant believes the Examiner's rejections should be withdrawn in view of the present amendment and arguments, submit specific supporting evidence or precise quotations from the cited references showing the asserted absence.
- If applicant elects to file further amendments or argument, do so promptly. Failure to respond within the statutory period will result in entry of a final action or abandonment in accordance with applicable rules.
Limitations and Evidence Uncertainty
- The Examiner's maintenance of the rejections in this communication is based on the prior Office action (IQV0V978RXEAPX0) that relied on Leech, Forest, and Savarese; the full text of those patents/applications is not included in the documents supplied with the A1-response in the present file record excerpt provided to the predictive assistant. Where applicant contends specific teaching or non-teaching in those references, applicant should identify specific passages in those references for the record.
- If applicant files additional evidence (reference excerpts, a declaration, or expert statements) or further claim amendments that clearly identify distinguishing subject matter, the Examiner will reconsider the outstanding rejections and respond in the next action.
Summary of Examiner Determination

Applicant's arguments and the claim amendments filed 10/24/2016 do not, on the present record, provide sufficient evidence or claim limitations that overcome the cited prior art combination. The Examiner invites applicant to submit specific citations, admissible evidence, or further amendments that substantively distinguish the claims from the cited references.
Next steps

applicant_argument_responses.argument_summary: Applicant argues Yamaguchi does not disclose "a plurality of individual detection units corresponding to movement directions of the object," and therefore does not anticipate claim 1. Applicant cites Yamaguchi paragraphs [0329]-[0335] and contends the cited art fails to show plurality corresponding to movement directions.
applicant_argument_responses.response: The examiner has reviewed paragraphs [0329]-[0335] of Yamaguchi as cited by Applicant. These passages describe push buttons and sensors that change indicated movement when the remote casing orientation varies (forward, backward, diagonal). The Office interprets the disclosure of FIGs. 22–23 and the accompanying text as teaching: (a) multiple detection elements (push buttons, optical sensors/baffles) and (b) association of specific detection outputs with movement directions of the controlled object (forward, backward, diagonal). Therefore Yamaguchi discloses detection units arranged to indicate different movement directions and detection of directional selection by the operator. Applicant’s argument is noted but does not persuasively distinguish the cited disclosure from the claim limitations. If Applicant believes specific claim language is not supported by the cited passages, Applicant should propose claim amendments to recite the precise structure relied upon or submit evidence that the cited passages do not teach the limitation. See cited Yamaguchi passages: "[0329] In FIG. 22(a)... optical sensor 92 is switched, which results in indication of movement in the forward direction A" and "[0331]... optical sensors 92 and 93 are switched... which results in indication of movement diagonally in the forward direction A."
applicant_argument_responses.support_span: [0329] In FIG. 22(a), when the push button 76 is pressed... optical sensor 92 is switched, which results in indication of movement in the forward direction A.; [0331] In contrast, in FIG. 23(a), when the push button 76 is pressed... optical sensors 92 and 93 are switched at the same time, which results in indication of movement diagonally in the forward direction A.

parsed.office_action:
Action on Claims and Grounds
Summary
This action responds to the applicant's A1 submission filed February 11, 2014 (documents HRJYYOX2PXXIFW3 et seq.) and considers the prior Office communication of record (CTNF dated October 11, 2013, HMKNOW2XPXXIFW4). Applicant canceled claims 2–4 and amended claim 1 and several dependents; replacement drawings and specification amendments were filed. The Office withdraws the earlier drawing objection regarding depiction of the driving device because the specification and figures of record show element 2 and Fig. 3 as a block diagram of the driving device and its control. The remaining rejections are maintained for the reasons below. This is a non-final Office action (CTNF).
Claims Pending
Entered claim set (as examined) included claims 1–9 (GYDG1G10…). Applicant filed a proposed amended claim listing (HRJYYOY0PXXIFW3) with cancellation of claims 2–4 and proposed amended and new claims 1, 5–11. The entry status of the proposed amended claims is not established by the record; the examiner has reviewed the application as originally entered and the applicant’s A1 submission. The Office treats the applicant’s cancellations as effective to remove claims 2–4 from further consideration. The amendments to claim 1 and other claims in A1 will be considered for entry if the applicant files the formal claim set in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 1.121 and the amendment is in condition for entry. At present the outstanding rejections apply to the claim scope of record, and to the pending claim as entered if the amendment is entered.
Drawings
Applicant argued that the drawing objection has been resolved by pointing to Fig. 3. Examiner note: the earlier drawing objection is withdrawn because the specification and figures of record (Fig. 3) show the driving device and motor control circuitry. Evidence: specification and Fig. 3 discussion (pgpub_description). If applicant elects to add new claim limitations that require particular drawing detail not present, corrected replacement sheets should be submitted as needed.
35 U.S.C. 112 (Clarity / Antecedent Basis)
Preliminary: Applicant cancelled claims 2–4. The Office’s prior 35 U.S.C. 112(b) objections to those dependent claim numbers are withdrawn as moot. If the applicant reintroduces the substance of those dependents in other claim form, antecedent and clarity will be re-evaluated.
Claim 1: Applicant incorporated previously-dependent material into claim 1 in the A1 filing. If applicant’s amended claim 1 is formally entered, the Office will examine claim 1 for compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112. Where applicant’s amendment uses terms such as “the detection unit” or “the jacket member,” sufficient antecedent support and precise definition of these elements must be present in the claim and in the specification. If claim 1 is entered and the Office finds lack of antecedent or indefiniteness, an explicit 112 objection will be issued identifying the precise claim wording at issue and the required clarification. At this time claims 2–4 are canceled and no 112 objection remains against those canceled claim numbers.
35 U.S.C. 102 / Anticipation
Claims 1, 5, 6, 8 and 9 (claims that depend or incorporate the features of claim 1) remain rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b) as anticipated by Yamaguchi (WO 2008/099611). The record shows that Yamaguchi teaches an operating device (remote control) with multiple detection elements (push buttons, baffles and optical sensors) and shows that different sensor outputs correspond to different indicated travel directions (examples include forward, backward, and diagonal directions as described in FIGS. 22 and 23 and paragraphs [0329]–[0335]). The examiner’s position is that the cited passages disclose multiple detection units arranged and operated to indicate or select movement directions of the controlled object, thereby meeting the claim limitations.
Applicant’s argument that Yamaguchi does not disclose “a plurality of individual detection units corresponding to movement directions of the object” has been considered. The specification passages in Yamaguchi cited by Applicant ([0329]–[0335]) describe push buttons and sensors which change the indicated movement when the casing orientation changes and when different push buttons or combinations are activated, including diagonals. The Office interprets that disclosure as disclosing multiple detection elements associated with different directions. Because anticipation requires that a single prior-art reference disclose each and every claimed element, and because the Office finds such disclosure in Yamaguchi, the anticipation rejection is maintained.
Applicant may respond by either (1) amending the claims to recite structure or limitations not found in the cited disclosure (for example, a particular physical arrangement, specific sensor type or particular claimed association), or (2) submitting persuasive evidence demonstrating that the cited passages do not teach the claimed limitation. If amendment is chosen, please submit a formal claim set under 37 C.F.R. § 1.121. If evidence is submitted, it should be documentary and explain why the cited passages are not reasonably read to disclose the limitation.
35 U.S.C. 103 / Obviousness
Claim 7 (illuminating device forming a light spot as a notification unit) remains rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) over Yamaguchi. The Office’s position is that Yamaguchi’s teaching of visual/optical signaling and direction indication renders it within the routine skill of the art to employ an illuminating spot to indicate travel direction to observers. Applicant has not submitted persuasive technical evidence of unexpected results or a showing that the prior art teaches away from an illuminating notification unit. The rejection is therefore maintained. To overcome the 103 rejection, applicant may amend the claims to include a particular configuration or function of the illuminating device that is not shown or suggested in Yamaguchi, or present experimental or documentary evidence that establishes non-obviousness.
Procedural and Entry Matters
Applicant submitted an amended claim listing (HRJYYOY0PXXIFW3) and amendments to the specification and drawings. The record does not establish formal entry of the amended claims. Applicant is advised to file a replacement formal claim set (with markings showing amendments) in compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 1.121 for prompt entry. If applicant wishes the examiner to consider the present amended claim text as the operative claim set, please submit a clear statement that the claims are being presented for entry along with a formal replacement claim set. If the amended claims are entered, the examiner will re-evaluate the rejections against the entered text and issue a further action as appropriate.
Conclusion and Requirements
1) The Office withdraws the earlier drawing objection concerning depiction of the driving device in view of Fig. 3 and the specification text. Applicant’s replacement drawing sheets are of record but formal corrected sheets should be submitted under 37 C.F.R. § 1.121 if not already in compliance.
2) Claims 2–4: the prior 35 U.S.C. 112 objections to those claim numbers are withdrawn because applicant canceled those claims. If applicant reintroduces these limitations in other claims, the Office will re-examine antecedent and clarity.
3) Claims 1, 5, 6, 8 and 9: the rejection under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b) over Yamaguchi is maintained. The examiner finds disclosure in the cited Yamaguchi passages of multiple detection elements and association of detection outputs with movement directions.
4) Claim 7: the rejection under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) over Yamaguchi is maintained.
5) Applicant may overcome the rejections by one or more of the following (preferably in a single reply): (a) submitting a formal replacement claim set for entry under 37 C.F.R. § 1.121 with any further amendments that distinguish over Yamaguchi, (b) amending claims to recite structural features not shown or suggested in Yamaguchi (supported by the specification), and/or (c) submitting persuasive documentary evidence (for example experimental data, declarations, or other printed publications) that the cited prior art does not disclose or render obvious the claimed features.
6) If applicant wishes to teleconference to discuss possible claim amendments and the cited references, contact the examiner to arrange a time (telephone number listed in the prior Office action). If applicant believes additional time is required to prepare a substantive reply, applicant may request an extension under 37 C.F.R. § 1.136. Any petition for extension should explain the reasons and include required fees.
Limitations
- Applicant’s A1 submission contains OCR and formatting errors in the proposed claim text; those errors create uncertainty whether the submitted amended claims were intended exactly as printed. The Office requires a clean, formal claim set for entry under 37 C.F.R. § 1.121. If applicant expects the examiner to consider the amended claim text, submit corrected formal claims.
- The examiner relies on the cited passages of Yamaguchi as supplied in the October 11, 2013 Office action (HMKNOW2XPXXIFW4). The examiner’s factual findings about disclosure are based on those passages in the record. If applicant submits additional prior art or documentary evidence beyond the cutoff, the Office will consider it as permitted under applicable rules.
Examiner: Michael E. Gallion, Art Unit 3654
limitations: Uncertainty whether applicant's messy OCR claim text in HRJYYOY0PXXIFW3 was intended as formally entered claims; applicant must file a clean replacement claim set under 37 C.F.R. §1.121 for entry.
Responses rely on Yamaguchi passages as printed in the October 11, 2013 Office action (HMKNOW2XPXXIFW4); if applicant submits further evidence, prosecution may be affected.
Canceled claims 2–4 withdraw earlier 112 objections as moot; if reintroduced, clarity/antecedent review will be required.

Applicant: (1) amended claims 11 and 20 to add an explicit closure-device limitation and (2) cancelled claims 15 and 16. This communication withdraws the prior rejections that depended upon the portions of Hooven relied upon in the February 5, 2014 Office action to the extent explained below, and explains the present status of pending claims. No new prior-art references are added in this communication.\n\nBackground (record and prior Office action)\nThe examiner’s February 5, 2014 Office action relied on Hooven (as characterized in the Office action) to reject claims 11–14, 17, and 20–23 under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b). Claims 21–24 depend from claim 20 and thus include the added closure-device limitation by dependency.\n- Office position: The February 5, 2014 Office action relied on passages in HR7RYP0UPXXIFW4 addressing access (for example, trans-septal access). The examiner agrees with Applicant that the trans-septal access described in the prior action is a different access technique than accessing the left atrium via puncture of the left atrial appendage. The characterization of Hooven in HR7RYP0UPXXIFW4 does not disclose a closure device comprising both a snare loop and a suture loop and its use to isolate the LAA. Accordingly, the prior 35 U.S.C. 102(b) rejection of claim 20 (and claims 21–24) which was premised on the record in HR7RYP0UPXXIFW4 is withdrawn as to the amended claim set.\n- Status: The prior 35 U.S.C. 102(b) rejection of claims 20–24 is withdrawn for the amended claims. Accordingly those combinations are withdrawn on the present record.\n\nProcedural notes / next steps\n- Election: Applicant’s prior provisional election (phone Jan. 9, 2014) remains of record and Applicant has affirmed that election in the response (HUUESM4ZPXXIFW3). If no such prior-art is located, the examiner will prepare an action consistent with the results of the prior-art review (which could be allowance if no grounds of rejection remain).\n\nSummary and disposition\n- Applicant’s amendment (HUUESM4ZPXXIFW3) adding a closure-device limitation and isolating step to claims 11 and 20 is acknowledged and has been considered. The examiner will perform additional searching and will mail an appropriate next action. If Applicant wishes to present any additional amendments or arguments at this time (for example, narrowing claim language further, or pointing the examiner to specific prior-art passages that Applicant believes remain dispositive), those may be filed in reply to this communication. If Applicant believes a telephone interview would expedite resolution, the examiner invites Applicant to request such an interview.\n\nLimitations\n- The examiner’s withdrawal of the prior rejections is based on the record in the cited Office action (HR7RYP0UPXXIFW4) and on the amended claims in HUUESM4ZPXXIFW3. No independent copy of Hooven was provided with the prior Office action in the file wrapper input documents available to the examiner for this response; the examiner relied on the characterization of Hooven as quoted in the prior Office action. If counsel provides specific passages from Hooven (or other prior art) not already in the record that disclose the claimed closure-device or LAA-puncture access as now claimed, the examiner will promptly consider that material and respond accordingly.\n\nExaminer\nEunhwa Kim\nArt Unit 3739\nContact phone: (571) 270-1265\n",

parsed.office_action:
Examiner Communication — Non-Final (Follow-up)

Summary
This communication follows Applicant’s Amendment filed May 5, 2014 (HUUESM4ZPXXIFW3) and the Office action mailed February 5, 2014 (HR7RYP0UPXXIFW4). Applicant: (1) amended claims 11 and 20 to add an explicit closure-device limitation and (2) cancelled claims 15 and 16. Applicant also affirmed the earlier provisional election (telephone, Jan. 9, 2014). This communication withdraws the prior rejections that depended upon the portions of Hooven relied upon in the February 5, 2014 Office action to the extent explained below, and explains the present status of pending claims. No new prior-art references are added in this communication.

Background (record and prior Office action)
The examiner’s February 5, 2014 Office action relied on Hooven (as characterized in the Office action) to reject claims 11–14, 17, and 20–23 under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b). The action also made 103 rejections for certain dependent claims in combination with other references. The February 5, 2014 action includes and quotes passages that summarize Hooven’s disclosure regarding endocardial/epicardial bodies and ablation, for example: "the electrodes can be activated for ablation by the ablation activation device. The tissue layer is ablated by the electrical connection between the electrodes disposed on opposite sides of the tissue layer" (HR7RYP0UPXXIFW4). The present applicant response (May 5, 2014) amended claims 11 and 20 to include an express limitation that a closure device comprising a snare loop and a suture loop is advanced to an external surface of a left atrial appendage and that the LAA is isolated with that closure device (HUUESM4ZPXXIFW3).

Claim-specific determinations in light of Applicant’s amendment
1) Claims 11–14 and 17 (amended claim 11 is the base):
- Amendment: Claim 11 now recites, in addition to the previously recited endocardial/epicardial ablation steps, "advancing a closure device comprising a snare loop and a suture loop to an external surface of a left atrial appendage; and isolating the left atrial appendage with the closure device." (HUUESM4ZPXXIFW3).
- Office position: The examiner has reviewed the prior rejection basis (HR7RYP0UPXXIFW4) and the passages quoted therein describing Hooven’s ablation bodies and electrode-based ablation. The quoted Hooven material establishes disclosure of paired devices that ablate tissue therebetween, but the prior action’s record (HR7RYP0UPXXIFW4) does not show that Hooven discloses advancing a closure device having both a snare loop and a suture loop and using that device to isolate the LAA. Therefore, on the present record the examiner withdraws the prior pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b) rejection of amended claim 11 and, accordingly, withdraws that 102(b) rejection as to claims 12–14 and 17 which depend from claim 11. The examiner recognizes Applicant’s argument that Hooven’s septal (trans-septal) access teaching is not equivalent to the claimed LAA puncture access and agrees that the record relied upon in the prior Office action does not establish that Hooven discloses the newly added closure-device and isolating limitations.
- Status: The prior 35 U.S.C. 102(b) rejection of claims 11–14 and 17 based on the characterization of Hooven in HR7RYP0UPXXIFW4 is withdrawn as to the amended claim set. If the Office identifies different or additional prior-art passages (from Hooven or another reference) that explicitly disclose the added closure-device and isolation steps, the examiner will place that material on the record and explain any renewed rejection.

2) Claims 20–24 (base claim 20 as amended):
- Amendment: Claim 20 now recites inter alia advancing a tissue-affecting device into the left atrium through a puncture in the left atrial appendage, and further recites isolating the LAA using an advancing closure device (the examiner notes Applicant’s correction of a minor typographical error in the amendment). Claims 21–24 depend from claim 20 and thus include the added closure-device limitation by dependency.
- Office position: The February 5, 2014 Office action relied on passages in HR7RYP0UPXXIFW4 addressing access (for example, trans-septal access). The examiner agrees with Applicant that the trans-septal access described in the prior action is a different access technique than accessing the left atrium via puncture of the left atrial appendage. The characterization of Hooven in HR7RYP0UPXXIFW4 does not disclose a closure device comprising both a snare loop and a suture loop and its use to isolate the LAA. Accordingly, the prior 35 U.S.C. 102(b) rejection of claim 20 (and claims 21–24) which was premised on the record in HR7RYP0UPXXIFW4 is withdrawn as to the amended claim set.
- Status: The prior 35 U.S.C. 102(b) rejection of claims 20–24 is withdrawn for the amended claims. As above, if a prior-art reference is located that explicitly discloses advancing a closure device with the recited snare-and-suture structure and isolating the LAA with that device, the examiner will place such material on the record with explanation.

3) Rejections under 35 U.S.C. 103 that relied on Hooven as the primary reference:
- Office position: Because the 102(b) rejections based on Hooven (as characterized in HR7RYP0UPXXIFW4) are withdrawn for the amended claims, the examiner has also withdrawn the corresponding 35 U.S.C. 103(a) rejections for those amended claims where the combination depended on Hooven as the primary reference and did not supply the added closure-device and isolation limitation. Where the Office has cited secondary references in an attempt to supply the missing limitation, the examiner finds the record presently before the Office insufficient to show that the secondary references alone or in combination actually disclose the exact closure device structure and use recited in the amended claims. Accordingly those combinations are withdrawn on the present record.

Procedural notes / next steps
- Election: Applicant’s prior provisional election (phone Jan. 9, 2014) remains of record and Applicant has affirmed that election in the response (HUUESM4ZPXXIFW3). That election is unaffected by the claim amendments.
- Claim formality: The prior claim-typing/spelling objection to claim 20 ("therebtween") has been addressed by Applicant’s corrected text and the objection is moot.
- New searches / potential further action: The examiner has withdrawn the prior rejections described above in light of Applicant’s amendments and arguments and the record as it exists. The examiner will perform further search(s) as necessary to determine whether any available prior-art reference(s) disclose the closure-device limitation (a closure device comprising a snare loop and a suture loop used to isolate the LAA) or the combination of LAA-puncture access plus the closure-device/isolation limitation. If such references are located they will be placed of record with an explanation and, if merited, appropriate rejections will be made. If no such prior-art is located, the examiner will prepare an action consistent with the results of the prior-art review (which could be allowance if no grounds of rejection remain).

Summary and disposition
- Applicant’s amendment (HUUESM4ZPXXIFW3) adding a closure-device limitation and isolating step to claims 11 and 20 is acknowledged and has been considered. Claims 11–14, 17 and 20–24, as amended, now include the added closure-device/isolation limitation by dependency.
- The examiner withdraws the February 5, 2014 35 U.S.C. 102(b) anticipation rejections of claims 11–14, 17 and 20–24 to the extent those rejections were premised on the characterization of Hooven set forth in HR7RYP0UPXXIFW4, because the cited portions do not disclose the closure-device with both a snare loop and a suture loop used to isolate the LAA as newly recited in the amended claims (see HUUESM4ZPXXIFW3). The corresponding 35 U.S.C. 103(a) rejections that relied on Hooven as the primary reference are likewise withdrawn as to those amended claims for the same reason.
- The withdrawn rejections are withdrawn without prejudice: if the Office locates prior-art patents or publications that do expressly disclose the specific closure device and isolating step (or an equivalent showing), or that otherwise render the amended claims unpatentable, the examiner will make that material of record with explanation in a subsequent Office action.

Action requested of Applicant
No further amendment is required to address the rejections discussed above. The examiner will perform additional searching and will mail an appropriate next action. If Applicant wishes to present any additional amendments or arguments at this time (for example, narrowing claim language further, or pointing the examiner to specific prior-art passages that Applicant believes remain dispositive), those may be filed in reply to this communication. If Applicant believes a telephone interview would expedite resolution, the examiner invites Applicant to request such an interview.

Limitations
- The examiner’s withdrawal of the prior rejections is based on the record in the cited Office action (HR7RYP0UPXXIFW4) and on the amended claims in HUUESM4ZPXXIFW3. No independent copy of Hooven was provided with the prior Office action in the file wrapper input documents available to the examiner for this response; the examiner relied on the characterization of Hooven as quoted in the prior Office action. If counsel provides specific passages from Hooven (or other prior art) not already in the record that disclose the claimed closure-device or LAA-puncture access as now claimed, the examiner will promptly consider that material and respond accordingly.

Examiner
Eunhwa Kim
Art Unit 3739
Contact phone: (571) 270-1265
